-- Title companies file signing requests for themselves. The ID scan and the
-- fee are required: omitting either refuses at decode time.
mutation createSigning(signerName: text 1..120, address: text 1..300, documents: [text <=200] 1..20, idScan: image <=10000000, fee: money USD, agencyBillingNotes: text <=2000 ? alias billingNotes, outOfState: bool ?):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'title_company'] else NOT_TITLE_COMPANY
  return insert signings { titleCompany: viewer, signerName, address, documents, idScan, fee, agencyBillingNotes, outOfState: outOfState ?? false }

-- Dispatchers and the owner assign a registered notary. Out-of-state papers
-- need an owner-approved notary.
mutation assignSigning(signing: signings, notary: principal):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_STAFF 'Only dispatch staff assign signings.'
  require exists roles[principal = notary, role = 'notary'] else NOT_A_NOTARY 'That principal is not a notary.'
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'requested' else BAD_STATUS 'Only requested signings can be assigned.'
  if s.outOfState:
    p = notaryProfiles[principal = notary] ! else NOT_APPROVED 'That notary is not approved for out-of-state papers.'
    require p.approvedOutOfState else NOT_APPROVED 'That notary is not approved for out-of-state papers.'
  update signings[signing] { notary, status: 'assigned' }
  return null

-- The assigned notary (or dispatch staff) records the signing.
mutation markSigned(signing: signings):
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'assigned' else BAD_STATUS 'Only assigned signings can be marked signed.'
  require s.notary = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_ASSIGNED 'Only the assigned notary or dispatch staff records the signing.'
  update signings[signing] { status: 'signed', signedAt: now }
  return null

-- Signed papers ship back within one day of signing; later returns refuse.
mutation markReturned(signing: signings):
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'signed' else BAD_STATUS 'Only signed signings can be marked returned.'
  require s.signedAt != null else BAD_STATUS 'This signing has no signing time.'
  require now <= s.signedAt + 24h else RETURN_OVERDUE 'Signed papers must ship back within one day of signing.'
  require s.notary = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_ASSIGNED 'Only the assigned notary or dispatch staff records the return.'
  update signings[signing] { status: 'returned', returnedAt: now }
  return null

-- Dispatch staff adjust the fee charged to the title company. Only the
-- agency owner may change the agency billing notes; the dispatcher may
-- still read them but cannot change them.
mutation updateBilling(signing: signings, fee: money USD, agencyBillingNotes: text <=2000 ? alias billingNotes):
  require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'dispatcher'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_STAFF 'Only dispatch staff edits billing.'
  s = signings[signing] ! else NOT_FOUND
  if agencyBillingNotes != s.agencyBillingNotes:
    require exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'owner'] else NOT_OWNER_NOTES 'Only the agency owner changes agency billing notes.'
  update signings[signing] { fee, agencyBillingNotes }
  return null

-- Live dispatch board: every caller sees exactly the rows (and columns)
-- their rules admit, newest arrivals last.
query board(c: cursor ?):
  return signings first 100 by .id after c

query signingDetail(signing: signings):
  return signings[signing]

  update <- .owner = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'ranger']
  online only

invariant stays.read only .owner = viewer or (exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'host'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'ranger'])
invariant vehicles.read only .owner = viewer or (exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'host'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'ranger'])
invariant vehicles.delete only (exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'host'] or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'ranger'])
invariant payments.read only .owner = viewer or exists roles[principal = viewer, role = 'ranger']

mutation provision(principal: principal, role: enum('camper', 'host', 'ranger')):
  require viewer = 'service:operator' else NOT_OPERATOR
  return upsert roles[principal] { principal, role }
query myRole():
  return roles[principal = viewer]
query serverTime():
  require exists roles[principal = viewer] else SIGN_IN
  return now
query siteBoard():
  require exists roles[principal = viewer] else SIGN_IN
  return sites first 200 by .id { id, name, kind, nightly, reason: .reason if .status = 'closed' else '', holdUntil: null, status: 'open' if .status = 'booked' and .holdUntil != null and now >= .holdUntil else .status, current: null }
query myBookings():
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  return stays where .owner = viewer first 200 by .id
query booking(id: stays):
  return stays[id]
query myPayments():
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  return payments where .owner = viewer first 200 by .id
query payment(stay: stays):
  return payments[stay = stay]
query plate(stay: stays):
  if staff() and not ranger():
    return null
  return first(vehicles where .stay = stay first 1 by .id)
query liveStays():
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  return stays first 200 by .id

mutation addSite(name: text 1..60, kind: enum('tent', 'RV'), nightly: int 100..50000):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(name)) >= 1 else NAME_REQUIRED
  return insert sites { name, kind, nightly, status: 'open', current: null, holdUntil: null, reason: '' }

mutation book(site: sites, arrival: time, nights: int 1..30, photo: image <=5000000):
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  s = sites[site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'open' or s.status = 'cleaned' or (s.status = 'booked' and s.holdUntil != null and now >= s.holdUntil) else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  require arrival >= now and arrival <= now + 365d else ARRIVAL_RANGE
  total = s.nightly * nights
  b = insert stays { owner: viewer, site, arrival, nights, total, deposit: s.nightly, status: 'booked', reason: '' }
  insert vehicles { owner: viewer, stay: b.id, photo }
  insert payments { owner: viewer, stay: b.id, charged: total, refunded: 0, forfeited: 0, reason: '' }
  update sites[site] { status: 'booked', current: b.id, holdUntil: arrival + 1d, reason: '' }
  return b

mutation cancel(stay: stays):
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.owner = viewer else PRIVATE_BOOKING
  require b.status = 'booked' else NOT_BOOKED
  require now < b.arrival + 1d else HOLD_EXPIRED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status != 'closed' else RANGER_REFUND_REQUIRED
  lost = b.deposit if b.arrival - now < 14d else 0
  update payments[stay = stay] { refunded: b.total - lost, forfeited: lost, reason: 'Camper cancellation' }
  update stays[stay] { status: 'cancelled', reason: 'Camper cancellation' }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'open', current: null, holdUntil: null }

mutation checkIn(stay: stays):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.status = 'booked' else NOT_BOOKED
  require now >= b.arrival else TOO_EARLY
  require now < b.arrival + 1d else HOLD_EXPIRED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'booked' and s.current = stay else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  update stays[stay] { status: 'occupied' }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'occupied', holdUntil: null }

mutation checkOut(stay: stays):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.status = 'occupied' else NOT_OCCUPIED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'occupied' and s.current = stay else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  update stays[stay] { status: 'completed' }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'dirty', current: null }

mutation clean(site: sites):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  s = sites[site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'dirty' else NOT_DIRTY
  update sites[site] { status: 'cleaned' }

mutation closeSite(site: sites, reason: text 3..500):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(reason)) >= 3 else REASON_REQUIRED
  s = sites[site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status != 'closed' else ALREADY_CLOSED
  update sites[site] { status: 'closed', reason }

mutation refundClosed(stay: stays, reason: text 3..500):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(reason)) >= 3 else REASON_REQUIRED
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'closed' else SITE_NOT_CLOSED
  require b.status = 'booked' or b.status = 'occupied' else NOT_REFUNDABLE
  update payments[stay = stay] { refunded: b.total, forfeited: 0, reason }
  update stays[stay] { status: 'refunded', reason }
  update sites[b.site] { current: null }

mutation evict(stay: stays, reason: text 3..500):
  require ranger() else RANGER_ONLY
  require len(trim(reason)) >= 3 else REASON_REQUIRED
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.status = 'occupied' else NOT_OCCUPIED
  s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require s.status = 'occupied' and s.current = stay else SITE_UNAVAILABLE
  update stays[stay] { status: 'evicted', reason }
  update sites[b.site] { status: 'dirty', current: null, reason }

job releaseNoShows():
  for b in stays:
    if b.status = 'booked' and now >= b.arrival + 1d:
      s = sites[b.site] ! else NOT_FOUND
      if s.status != 'closed':
        update stays[b.id] { status: 'released', reason: 'No check-in within one day' }
        if s.current = b.id and s.status = 'booked':
          update sites[b.site] { status: 'open', current: null, holdUntil: null }

schedule noShowSweep every 1m: releaseNoShows

query vehiclesForBooking(stay: stays):
  return vehicles where .stay = stay first 200 by .id
mutation addVehicle(stay: stays, photo: image <=5000000):
  require camper() else CAMPER_ONLY
  b = stays[stay] ! else NOT_FOUND
  require b.owner = viewer else PRIVATE_BOOKING
  return insert vehicles {owner: viewer, stay, photo}
mutation removeVehicle(vehicle: vehicles):
  require staff() else STAFF_ONLY
  delete vehicles[vehicle]

// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#169-day-two-precision-and-destructive-evidence-questions — optionality alone is not mandatory evidence.
fn conjuncts(rule:&RuleExpr)->Vec<&RuleExpr>{match rule{RuleExpr::And(xs)=>xs.iter().flat_map(conjuncts).collect(),_=>vec![rule]}}
fn required_media(bound:&Bound,table:&str,column:&str)->bool{
    fn nonnull(rule:&RuleExpr,column:&str)->bool{
        let pair=match rule{RuleExpr::Ne(a,b)=>Some((a,b)),RuleExpr::Not(r)=>if let RuleExpr::Eq(a,b)=r.as_ref(){Some((a,b))}else{None},_=>None};
        pair.is_some_and(|(a,b)|[(a,b),(b,a)].iter().any(|(a,b)|matches!(a,RuleTerm::Field(c) if c==column)&&matches!(b,RuleTerm::Literal(snapback4_core::Value::Null))))
    }
    fn mandatory(kind:&ColumnType)->bool{match kind{ColumnType::Image{..}|ColumnType::File{..}|ColumnType::Video{..}=>true,ColumnType::ListRange{of,min,..}=>*min>0&&mandatory(of),_=>false}}
    mandatory(&bound.schema.tables[table].columns[column])||bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|i.table==table&&i.target=="always").filter_map(|i|i.policy.as_ref()).flat_map(conjuncts).any(|r|nonnull(r,column))
}
fn approves(w:&Write<'_>,bound:&Bound)->bool{
    w.fields.iter().any(|f|match field_value(f){
        Some(Expr::Literal{value:ast::Literal::Str(v),..})=>matches!(bound.schema.tables[&w.table].columns.get(&f.name).map(ColumnType::required),Some(ColumnType::Enum{..}))&&["approved","accepted","authorized","granted","issued","active","confirmed","paid","signed"].contains(&v.as_str()),
        Some(Expr::Literal{value:ast::Literal::Bool(true),..})=>["approv","authoriz"].iter().any(|part|f.name.to_lowercase().contains(part)),_=>false,
    })
}
fn stale_notes(bound:&Bound,writes:&[Write<'_>],out:&mut Vec<Diagnostic>){
    let mut groups=BTreeMap::<(String,String),(Site,BTreeSet<String>,BTreeSet<String>,BTreeSet<String>)>::new();
    for w in writes.iter().filter(|w|matches!(w.op,WriteOp::Insert|WriteOp::Upsert)){
        let mut dependencies=BTreeMap::<String,BTreeSet<String>>::new();
        for condition in conditions(&w.context){walk(condition,|e|match e{
            Expr::Member{base,name,..}=>for dep in reads(base){if dep!=w.table&&super::privilege::role_columns(bound,&dep).is_empty()&&bound.schema.tables.get(&dep).is_some_and(|t|t.columns.contains_key(name)&&!t.immutable_fields().any(|c|c==name))&&writes.iter().any(|o|o.table==dep&&(o.op==WriteOp::Delete||matches!(o.op,WriteOp::Update|WriteOp::Upsert)&&o.fields.iter().any(|f|&f.name==name))){dependencies.entry(dep).or_default().insert(name.clone());}},
            Expr::Exists{read,..} if read.table!=w.table&&super::privilege::role_columns(bound,&read.table).is_empty()&&writes.iter().any(|o|o.table==read.table&&o.op==WriteOp::Delete)=>{dependencies.entry(read.table.clone()).or_default().insert("existence".into());},_=>{},
        });}
        for (dep,columns) in dependencies{for later in writes.iter().filter(|o|o.p.name!=w.p.name&&approves(o,bound)&&(o.table==w.table&&o.op==WriteOp::Update||matches!(o.op,WriteOp::Insert|WriteOp::Upsert)&&bound.schema.tables[&o.table].columns.values().any(|k|matches!(k.required(),ColumnType::Ref{table} if table==&w.table)))){
            let mut rechecked=false;
            for condition in conditions(&later.context){walk(condition,|e|match e{
                Expr::Member{base,name,..} if columns.contains(name)&&reads(base).contains(&dep)=>rechecked=true,
                Expr::Exists{read,..} if read.table==dep&&(columns.contains("existence")||read.keys.iter().any(|k|k.column.as_ref().is_some_and(|c|columns.contains(c))))=>rechecked=true,_=>{},
            });}
            if rechecked{continue;}
            let g=groups.entry((w.table.clone(),dep.clone())).or_insert_with(||(later.site.clone(),BTreeSet::new(),BTreeSet::new(),BTreeSet::new()));
            if (&later.site.file,later.site.line,later.site.col)<(&g.0.file,g.0.line,g.0.col){g.0=later.site.clone();}
            g.1.insert(format!("{} at {}",w.p.name,w.site));g.2.insert(format!("{} at {}",later.p.name,later.site));g.3.extend(columns.clone());
        }}
    }
    for ((table,dep),(site,creators,decisions,columns)) in groups{note(out,&site,"N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK",format!("{table}: creation by {} checks mutable {dep}.{}, but approval/activation {} does not recheck it",creators.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "),columns.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(","),decisions.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),"decide whether eligibility must remain current at this decision; recheck it or declare independent intent and test create -> eligibility change -> approval");}
}
//! Real operation histories from a complete trusted fixture, including assets.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#122-reproducible-campaigns-and-reachability — only actual fixture traces establish application reachability.
use super::*;
const LIMIT:usize=512;
#[derive(Clone,Debug,Serialize,serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct Step {pub operation:String,pub viewer:String,pub args:BTreeMap<String,Value>,pub result:serde_json::Value}

pub(super) fn viewers(bound:&Bound)->Vec<String>{
    let mut out=BTreeSet::from([VIEWER.into(),OTHER.into(),"account:security-no-role".into(),"service:security".into()]);
    out.extend(bound.personas.iter().map(|p|if p.contains(':'){p.clone()}else{format!("dev:{p}")}));
    fn seats(value:&serde_json::Value,out:&mut BTreeSet<String>){match value{
        serde_json::Value::String(s) if s.starts_with("service:")&&s.len()>8=>{out.insert(s.clone());},
        serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs{seats(x,out)},
        serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for x in xs.values(){seats(x,out)},_=>{}
    }}
    seats(&serde_json::to_value(&bound.schema).unwrap(),&mut out);
    for p in &bound.programs{seats(&serde_json::to_value(&p.program).unwrap(),&mut out);}
    seats(&serde_json::to_value(&bound.invariants).unwrap(),&mut out);
    out.into_iter().collect()
}
pub(super) fn actors(bound:&Bound,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>)->Vec<String>{
    let mut out=viewers(bound);
    for (table,rs) in rows{for row in rs{for (c,k) in &bound.schema.tables[table].columns{
        if matches!(k.required(),C::Principal)&&let Ok(Value::Id(p))=row.field(c)&&!out.contains(p){out.push(p.clone());}
    }}}
    out
}
pub(super) fn fixture_cases(bound:&Bound,p:&Program,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,actors:&[String],out:&mut Campaign)->Vec<BTreeMap<String,Value>>{
    let args=&p.args;
    let mut literals=BTreeMap::<String,Vec<Value>>::new();
    fn collect(value:&serde_json::Value,out:&mut BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>){
        if let Some(binary)=value.get("Binary") {for (a,b) in [("left","right"),("right","left")] {
            if let (Some(name),Some(literal))=(binary.get(a).and_then(|v|v.get("Variable")).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),binary.get(b).and_then(|v|v.get("Literal"))) {
                if let Ok(value)=serde_json::from_value::<Value>(literal.clone()){out.entry(name.into()).or_default().push(value);}
            }
        }}
        match value{serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for v in xs.values(){collect(v,out)},serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for v in xs{collect(v,out)},_=>{}}
    }
    collect(&serde_json::to_value(p).unwrap(),&mut literals);
    fn values(name:&str,k:&ir::ArgType,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,actors:&[String])->Option<Vec<Value>>{
        Some(match k{
            ir::ArgType::Enum{variants}=>variants.iter().map(|s|Value::String(s.clone())).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Text{min,max,..}=>['z','y'].into_iter().map(|c|Value::String(c.to_string().repeat((*min).max(1).min(*max) as usize))).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Int=>vec![Value::Int(0),Value::Int(1),Value::Int(2)],
            ir::ArgType::IntRange{min,max}=>{let mut xs=vec![*min,1i64.clamp(*min,*max),*max];xs.sort();xs.dedup();xs.into_iter().map(Value::Int).collect()},
            ir::ArgType::Bool=>vec![Value::Bool(false),Value::Bool(true)],
            ir::ArgType::Time=>vec![Value::Int(NOW-86_400_000),Value::Int(NOW),Value::Int(NOW+86_400_000)],
            ir::ArgType::Principal=>actors.iter().map(|s|Value::Id(s.clone())).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Ref{table} if rows.get(table).is_some_and(|rs|!rs.is_empty())=>rows[table].iter().filter_map(|r|r.field("id").ok().cloned()).collect(),
            ir::ArgType::Optional(inner)=>{let mut v=vec![Value::Null];v.extend(values(name,inner,rows,actors)?);v},
            _=>vec![arguments(&BTreeMap::from([(name.into(),k.clone())]),0)?.remove(name)?],
        })
    }
    let mut cases=vec![BTreeMap::new()];
    for (name,k) in args{
        let Some(mut vals)=values(name,k,rows,actors)else{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{name}: history needs a typed asset argument"));return Vec::new();};
        for literal in literals.get(name).into_iter().flatten() {
            let valid=match (k,literal){
                (ir::ArgType::Text{min,max,..},Value::String(s))=>s.chars().filter(|c|!c.is_whitespace()).count()>=*min as usize&&s.chars().count()<=*max as usize,
                (ir::ArgType::Int,Value::Int(_))=>true,
                (ir::ArgType::IntRange{min,max},Value::Int(n))=>(*min..=*max).contains(n),_=>false,
            };
            if valid&&!vals.contains(literal){vals.insert(0,literal.clone());}
        }
        let mut next=Vec::new();
        'product:for offset in 0..vals.len(){for n in 0..cases.len().max(vals.len()){
            if out.exhausted(){return next;}
            let mut case=cases[n%cases.len()].clone();case.insert(name.clone(),vals[(n+offset)%vals.len()].clone());
            if !next.contains(&case){next.push(case);}if next.len()==LIMIT{out.unsupported.insert("history arguments capped at 512 combinations".into());break 'product;}
        }}
        cases=next;
    }
    let focused=super::executed::write_arguments(bound,p).into_iter().filter(|a|matches!(p.args.get(a),Some(ir::ArgType::Optional(_)))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if focused.is_empty(){return cases;}
    let mut prioritized=Vec::new();
    for case in cases{
        for name in &focused{if let Some(value)=arguments(&BTreeMap::from([(name.clone(),p.args[name].clone())]),4).and_then(|mut a|a.remove(name))&&value!=Value::Null{
            let mut alternate=case.clone();alternate.insert(name.clone(),value);if !prioritized.contains(&alternate){prioritized.push(alternate);}
        }}
        if !prioritized.contains(&case){prioritized.push(case.clone());}
        if prioritized.len()>=LIMIT{prioritized.truncate(LIMIT);out.unsupported.insert("column-write argument frontier capped at 512; remaining combinations uncovered".into());break;}
    }prioritized
}
// Preserve status/decision alternatives on each resource tuple before the
// small directed cap; text/noise arguments must not correlate bools with ids.
fn directed_cases(p:&Program,cases:Vec<BTreeMap<String,Value>>,campaign:&mut Campaign)->Vec<BTreeMap<String,Value>>{
    let identities=p.args.iter().filter(|(_,k)|matches!(k,ir::ArgType::Ref{..}|ir::ArgType::Principal)).map(|(n,_)|n).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let original=cases.clone();
    let mut seen=BTreeSet::new();let mut groups=Vec::new();
    for base in cases{let key=serde_json::to_string(&identities.iter().map(|n|(*n,base.get(*n))).collect::<Vec<_>>()).unwrap();if !seen.insert(key){continue;}
        let mut group=vec![base.clone()];
        for (name,kind) in &p.args{let values=match kind{ir::ArgType::Bool=>vec![Value::Bool(false),Value::Bool(true)],ir::ArgType::Enum{variants}=>variants.iter().cloned().map(Value::String).collect(),_=>Vec::new()};
            for value in values{let mut candidate=base.clone();candidate.insert(name.clone(),value);if !group.contains(&candidate){group.push(candidate);}}
        }groups.push(group);
    }
    let mut out=Vec::new();for n in 0..groups.iter().map(Vec::len).max().unwrap_or(0){for group in &groups{if let Some(args)=group.get(n){out.push(args.clone());}}}
    if original.iter().any(|case|!out.contains(case)){campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: directed argument grouping omits correlated/non-status alternatives; remaining combinations uncovered",p.name));}
    out
}
pub(super) fn trace_key(steps:&[Step])->Vec<(&str,&str)>{steps.iter().map(|s|(s.operation.as_str(),s.viewer.as_str())).collect()}
//! Individually justified source-bound dispositions; never proof or authority.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#162-narrow-gates-and-individual-dispositions — bulk compiler-note review cannot clear security gates.
use super::*;
use serde::{Serialize,Deserialize};
use sha2::{Digest,Sha256};
const ANALYZER:&str="sec7-3";
#[derive(Serialize,Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct File{version:u32,entries:BTreeMap<String,Entry>}
#[derive(Serialize,Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
struct Entry{sources:String,analyzer:String,reason:String}
#[derive(Serialize)]
pub(super) struct Disposition{pub id:String,pub code:String,pub site:String,pub gated:bool,pub acknowledged:bool,pub reason:Option<String>}
pub(super) fn gated(code:&str)->bool{matches!(code,"N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT"|"N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE")}
fn hash(bytes:&[u8])->String{format!("{:x}",Sha256::digest(bytes))}
fn digest(s:&str)->bool{s.len()==64&&s.bytes().all(|b|b.is_ascii_hexdigit())}
fn id(n:&snapback4_lang::Diagnostic)->String{hash(&serde_json::to_vec(&serde_json::to_value(n).unwrap()).unwrap())}
pub(super) fn review(project:&Project,sources:&[(String,String)],notes:&[snapback4_lang::Diagnostic],ack:Option<(&str,&str)>)->Result<Vec<Disposition>,String>{
    if project.sources().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?!=sources{return Err("Quarry sources changed during security review; rerun check".into());}
    let mut sorted=sources.to_vec();sorted.sort_by(|a,b|a.0.cmp(&b.0));
    let fingerprint=hash(&serde_json::to_vec(&sorted).unwrap());
    let path=project.schema_dir().join("security-reviews.json");
    // Keep the lock inode in ignored generated output. Do not unlink a lock
    // while another process can be waiting on that inode. Kernel ownership
    // releases it on exit, including an interrupted writer.
    let _writer_lock=if ack.is_some(){
        let directory=project.schema_dir().join("generated");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&directory).map_err(|e|format!("cannot create security review lock directory: {e}"))?;
        let lock=std::fs::OpenOptions::new().create(true).truncate(false).read(true).write(true).open(directory.join("security-reviews.lock")).map_err(|e|format!("cannot open security review lock: {e}"))?;
        lock.lock().map_err(|e|format!("cannot acquire security review lock: {e}"))?;Some(lock)
    }else{None};
    if project.sources().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?!=sources{return Err("Quarry sources changed while waiting for security review; rerun check".into());}
    let mut file:File=match std::fs::read(&path){
        Ok(bytes)=>serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|_|"invalid snapback/security-reviews.json; expected version 1 with per-note source/analyzer/reason records".to_string())?,
        Err(e) if e.kind()==std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound=>File{version:1,entries:BTreeMap::new()},
        Err(e)=>return Err(format!("cannot read security dispositions: {e}")),
    };
    if file.version!=1||file.entries.iter().any(|(key,e)|!digest(key)||!digest(&e.sources)||e.reason.trim().is_empty()||e.analyzer.is_empty()){return Err("invalid security disposition version/digest/reason".into());}
    if let Some((key,reason))=ack{
        if reason.trim().is_empty(){return Err("--reason needs the specification rationale for this individual note".into());}
        if !notes.iter().any(|n|id(n)==key){return Err("--ack-security ID is not a current security note; run check --json".into());}
        file.entries.insert(key.into(),Entry{sources:fingerprint.clone(),analyzer:ANALYZER.into(),reason:reason.trim().into()});
        let temporary=path.with_extension(format!("json.{}.tmp",std::process::id()));
        let result=std::fs::write(&temporary,serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&file).unwrap()).and_then(|_|{
            if project.sources()?!=sources{return Err(std::io::Error::other("Quarry sources changed before disposition publication; rerun check"));}
            std::fs::rename(&temporary,&path)
        });
        if let Err(e)=result{let _=std::fs::remove_file(&temporary);return Err(format!("cannot record security disposition: {e}"));}
    }
    Ok(notes.iter().map(|n|{let key=id(n);let entry=file.entries.get(&key).filter(|e|e.sources==fingerprint&&e.analyzer==ANALYZER);
        Disposition{id:key,code:n.code.clone(),site:n.site.to_string(),gated:gated(&n.code),acknowledged:entry.is_some(),reason:entry.map(|e|e.reason.clone())}
    }).collect())
}
pub(super) fn pending(dispositions:&[Disposition])->bool{dispositions.iter().any(|d|d.gated&&!d.acknowledged)}
pub(super) fn print(dispositions:&[Disposition]){for d in dispositions.iter().filter(|d|d.gated||d.acknowledged){
    if d.acknowledged{println!("security reviewed {} {}: {}",d.id,d.code,d.reason.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));}
    else{println!("security review required {} {} at {}; repair or check --ack-security {} --reason '<spec rationale>'",d.id,d.code,d.site,d.id);}
}}

//! Mutable syntax traversal shared by planning and final index-name resolution.
use crate::ast::*;

pub(crate) fn expression(value: &mut Expr, visit: &mut impl FnMut(&mut Expr)) {
    match value {
        Expr::Read(read) | Expr::Exists { read, .. } | Expr::Created { read, .. } => read_children(read, visit),
        Expr::Unary { value, .. } | Expr::Member { base: value, .. } | Expr::Assert { value, .. } | Expr::ShapeUse { base: value, .. } => expression(value, visit),
        Expr::Binary { left, right, .. } => { expression(left, visit); expression(right, visit); }
        Expr::Array { items, .. } | Expr::Call { args: items, .. } => { for item in items { expression(item, visit); } }
        Expr::Object { fields, .. } => { for field in fields { if let Some(value) = &mut field.value { expression(value, visit); } } }
        Expr::Shape { base, fields, .. } => { expression(base, visit); shape(fields, visit); }
        Expr::If { then, condition, otherwise, .. } => { expression(then, visit); expression(condition, visit); expression(otherwise, visit); }
        Expr::Walk { seed, .. } => expression(seed, visit),
        Expr::Write { keys, fields, condition, .. } => {
            for key in keys { expression(&mut key.value, visit); }
            for field in fields { if let Some(value) = &mut field.value { expression(value, visit); } }
            if let Some(value) = condition { expression(value, visit); }
        }
        Expr::Merge(merge) => {
            for value in [&mut merge.matching, &mut merge.filter, &mut merge.cursor].into_iter().flatten() { expression(value, visit); }
            let mut lanes = Vec::new();
            for mut lane in std::mem::take(&mut merge.lanes) {
                if let Some(predicate) = &mut lane.admission { expression(predicate, visit); }
                if let Some((_, read)) = &mut lane.nulls {
                    let mut value = Expr::Read(*read.clone());
                    expression(&mut value, visit);
                    let Expr::Read(planned) = value else { unreachable!("planned null scan") };
                    **read = planned;
                }
                if let Some(value) = &mut lane.distinct { expression(value, visit); }
                if let Some(fields) = &mut lane.project { shape(fields, visit); }
                for value in &mut lane.prefix { expression(value, visit); }
                if let Some((_, value)) = &mut lane.loop_ { expression(value, visit); }
                if let Some(read) = &mut lane.planned {
                    let mut value = Expr::Read(*read.clone());
                    expression(&mut value, visit);
                    match value {
                        Expr::Read(planned) => **read = planned,
                        Expr::Merge(nested) if lane.loop_.is_none() => {
                            for mut child in nested.lanes {
                                child.branch = lane.branch.clone();
                                child.project = lane.project.clone();
                                lanes.push(child);
                            }
                            continue;
                        }
                        _ => unreachable!("a planned lane is a read or an expanded read"),
                    }
                }
                lanes.push(lane);
            }
            merge.lanes = lanes;
        }
        Expr::Name { .. } | Expr::Focal { .. } | Expr::Literal { .. } => {}
    }
    visit(value);
}

fn read_children(read: &mut ReadExpr, visit: &mut impl FnMut(&mut Expr)) {
    for key in &mut read.keys { expression(&mut key.value, visit); }
    for seek in &mut read.seeks { expression(&mut seek.value, visit); }
    for value in [&mut read.filter, &mut read.matching].into_iter().flatten() { expression(value, visit); }
    if let Some(value) = read.range.as_mut().and_then(|range| range.cursor.as_mut()) { expression(value, visit); }
}

pub(super) fn shape(fields: &mut [ShapeField], visit: &mut impl FnMut(&mut Expr)) {
    for field in fields { if let ShapeField::Field { value, .. } = field { expression(value, visit); } }
}

pub(super) fn statements(body: &mut [Stmt], visit: &mut impl FnMut(&mut Expr)) {
    for stmt in body {
        match stmt {
            Stmt::Bind { value, .. } | Stmt::Expr { value, .. } | Stmt::Return { value, .. } => expression(value, visit),
            Stmt::Require { condition, .. } => expression(condition, visit),
            Stmt::Emit { payload, once, .. } => {
                expression(payload, visit);
                if let Some(key) = once { expression(key, visit); }
            }
            Stmt::If { condition, then_body, else_body, .. } => { expression(condition, visit); statements(then_body, visit); statements(else_body, visit); }
            Stmt::As { principal: domain, body, .. } | Stmt::For { domain, body, .. } => { expression(domain, visit); statements(body, visit); }
            Stmt::Break { .. } | Stmt::Continue { .. } => {}
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) fn document(doc: &mut Document, visit: &mut impl FnMut(&mut Expr)) {
    // @ref LLP 3000.000.000.002#8-wave-21-release-evolution — historical lookups receive the same predicate/index planning as ordinary reads.
    for fill in doc.backfills.iter_mut().chain(&mut doc.downfills) {expression(&mut fill.value,visit);}

    for program in &mut doc.programs { statements(&mut program.prelude, visit); statements(&mut program.body, visit); }
    for function in &mut doc.functions {
        match &mut function.body { FunctionBody::Expression(value) => expression(value, visit), FunctionBody::Block(body) => statements(body, visit) }
    }
    for decl in &mut doc.shapes { shape(&mut decl.fields, visit); }
}

insert/update/delete against that transaction's current snapshot. Updates judge
old and next images; column updates (whether targeted by `write only` or `update only`) require an actual column change. No-op and
if-absent collision arms are not inserted writes. The trace includes intermediate
writes subsequently overwritten, loops, and delete/reinsert. Only a committed
ordinary authored operation contributes failure-eligible evidence; a rolled-back
operation contributes no write violation. Seed/synthetic origins retain their
non-failing classification. Unknown/error judgments are coverage gaps.
Instrumentation has a separate reader and meter, cannot alter product admission,
and is unavailable on the wire and the web device. No finite trace proves intent.
The hook is Context::with_fixture_trace, absent by default and not deserialized.
The physical insert/replace/delete primitives invoke it after authorization and
validation, before their store write. Collision/no-op branches never reach it;
upsert arm identity follows the primitive actually executed, not write_tables.
It creates a fresh Runner over the same provisional transaction with a separate
unbounded meter, authorization budget, caches and observation state. It does not
change the application Runner or serialize anything into its outcome. A Created
predicate is unknown until created-fact instrumentation is supported. The caller
discards the entire trace unless mutate returns Sent. Policy errors never alter
the product result. Implicit effects without an instrumented boundary remain
explicitly uncovered. Such missing hooks do not invalidate neighboring instantaneous
judgments, but every cross-boundary stability claim inherits §12.8's transitive
implicit-target and read-authority-dependency closure. No new kernel axiom.

### 15.2 Mutation results are observations

Column privacy includes implicit write results, explicit return objects and
authored refusals. A query projection is only one observer's shape. Located
no-invariant advice identifies columns omitted from an authored query projection
or guarded by a column rule that another authored result/refusal may observe.
It names the operation and column and asks for independent spec intent; it does
not claim that every returned private column violates the intended audience.

Actual compiler-typed mutation row payloads are checked against column read
intent as queries are. This reduction requires a stable necessary policy across
the mutation and a surviving committed image; ambiguous intermediate/changed
policy (using §12.8 and stability::implicit/dependencies closures), derived values or refusal dependencies require existing paired-world
replay or remain uncovered. Equal scalar values alone are not source provenance.
Hidden/omitted payloads and safe projections must not create a failure.
For a typed returned row, all row-local policy operands (including reference
source columns) must be present and equal to the judged committed image. A
saved readable row returned after its owner changes is uncovered, not refuted
against the new owner. External rule/read-authority dependencies must remain
unchanged through the transitive closure. The captured server clock is injected
into instrumented judgment images as in existing fixture_policy replay.
Declared read intent constrains actual typed output even for insertion echoes;
a creator's supplied or copied values are not an implicit privacy exemption.
Three prior query-coupling controls returned their protected field from a writer;
retain their query intent but project writer ids, and separately assert the old
full-row returns now refute. No weakening of the independent invariant. The reviewed direct runtime reductions are WriteTarget's final ordinary get
followed by columns::write_result, and insertion's ProjectFields builtin using
project_row_if_readable with column rules. Explicit return expressions consume
already projected authored values. Refusal and derived paths are not claimed to
be universally reduced by those two cases: paired observers and explicit blockers
remain. Regress both server insertion and server update result redaction. This
work never treats a query projection as an authorization rule.

The insert-intent and result-exposure review notes remain visible in short `check` output outside the ordinary note cap, following the existing escalation precedent. Nullable creation arguments retain null-first population coverage; direct optional column-write challenges interleave non-null alternatives within the existing finite cap. Missing commit-end images from expiry report coverage only and never stand in for an executed delete.

### 15.3 Rule-changing deployment review

Both deploy and deploy --check lead with outstanding security review items when
bound row/column/owner rules change against the selected live release (including
added/deleted tables). Print every refuted/unproved declaration and each security
note without an ordinary note cap, with source, reason, repair/next command.
Display the last recorded test time, age, completion, reachable violations and
coverage gaps; identify stale source/fixture/CLI evidence explicitly. No record
means never tested, not passed. Matching tests remain finite evidence, not proof.
Timestamp metadata is outside the input fingerprint. Record latest-run time and
outcome separately from last-completed-campaign time; an incomplete run may update
the former but never refresh the latter. Persist optional timestamps with
existing input-bound records;
legacy records say age unknown rather than inventing a date. A later incomplete
run cannot erase earlier established refutations on the same inputs.

Ordinary deploy remains advisory. Explicit --strict refuses rule-changing
previews and activation on failure-eligible reachable refutations (fresh bounded
analysis or matching persisted evidence), before any activation. Analysis, persisted evidence and narration resolve the
same saved-source companion fixtures once (an explicit --fixture overrides). Unproved items,
notes, stale evidence and synthetic-only refutations are not strict refusals.
Matching persisted eligible failures suffice even when bounded resampling is
skipped; skipped work is never described as fresh exploration. Refutations lead
the text; unproved declarations are one line per target and notes follow, avoiding
large per-obligation expansions. Keep all items visible as the author requested.
No stricter meaning is attached to passing finite tests. JSON retains the review
text and stderr prominently prints it; no preview/private snapshot mutates live
release data. Review follows the selected saved source and fixtures.

### 15.4 Supplied client sessions

Online and local constructors validate a supplied session before any transport,
device/storage work or timer. Require a non-array object with nonempty principal,
kind and token strings, a positive finite safe-integer expiresAt in milliseconds,
and valid optional scope/capExpiresAt fields. Legacy scope-less sessions remain
accepted. Expiry relative to a possibly skewed local clock is server authority;
shape validation must not reject a structurally valid past timestamp. Malformed
input throws E_SESSION with the offending field and a repair: pass the complete
Session returned by guest/login/signup or service minting, or use the existing
online token option for a bare bearer. Never include credentials in the error.
capExpiresAt without scope remains accepted legacy metadata; neither grants read authority.
Stored-session validation retains its existing auth restore path. Snapshot validated primitive fields so caller mutation cannot manufacture a NaN
timer later. Existing intentional full-session refresh and read/action expiry
semantics remain unchanged; shape validation grants no authority.

//! CLI security reporting; compile/test evidence share one analyzer.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#5-exposure-report — full audit is opt-in, intent notes are on ordinary check.
use super::*;
use snapback4_lang::security::{self,Report};
mod http;
mod record;
pub(super) use record::{remember,capture};
pub(super) fn unauthenticated(bound:&Bound,sources:&[(String,String)])->bool {
    match http::run(bound,sources){Ok(_)=>true,Err(why)=>{eprintln!("security HTTP failure: {why}");false}}
}
pub(super) fn report(project:&Project,bound:&Bound,sources:&[(String,String)],options:&Options)->Report{
    let mut selection=options.clone();
    let selected_fixture=record::selected_fixture(project,options);
    if selected_fixture.is_dir(){selection.flags.insert("fixture".into(),selected_fixture.to_string_lossy().into_owned());}
    let inputs=match selection.flags.get("fixture"){
        Some(path)=>match super::test_fixture::snapshot(std::path::Path::new(path)){Ok(snapshot)=>Some(snapshot),Err(why)=>{let mut report=security::analyze_rules(bound);security::add_source_notes(&mut report,sources,bound);report.campaign_coverage.insert(format!("fixture reachability not covered: {why}"));return report;}},None=>None,
    };
    if let Some(snapshot)=&inputs{selection.flags.insert("fixture".into(),snapshot.0.to_string_lossy().into_owned());}
    let cached=record::matching(project,&selection,sources);
    let known_failure=cached.as_ref().is_some_and(|r|!r.violations.is_empty())&&!options.flags.contains_key("security-full");
    let mut campaign=if options.flags.contains_key("security-full"){security::challenges::Campaign::default()}else{security::challenges::Campaign::bounded(1500)};
    if known_failure {campaign.work_remaining=Some(0);campaign.unsupported.insert("matching full-test refutations retained; bounded resampling skipped; repair and rerun snapback4 test".into());}
    // An explicitly selected fixture remains the initial-state assumption.
    // Static generation runs only on the fixture-free path; both share this
    // one bounded campaign with all subsequent concrete exploration.
    let mut report=if selection.flags.contains_key("fixture")||known_failure{
        security::analyze_rules(bound)
    }else{security::analyze_with_campaign(bound,&mut campaign)};
    security::add_source_notes(&mut report,sources,bound);
    if !bound.invariants.is_empty()&&!known_failure{
        if selection.flags.contains_key("fixture"){
            match super::test_fixture::engine_at(project,bound,&selection,1_800_000_000_000){
                Ok(fixture)=>if bound.schema.tables.keys().any(|t|fixture.store().rows(t).is_ok_and(|rs|!rs.is_empty())){security::challenges::fixture_observers(bound,&fixture,&mut campaign)}else{
                    // An empty starter directory selects generation, just as
                    // no fixture does. Give the direct contradiction its turn
                    // before empty-start mutation permutations spend the cap.
                    report=security::analyze_with_campaign(bound,&mut campaign);
                    security::add_source_notes(&mut report,sources,bound);
                    security::challenges::generated_campaign(bound,&mut campaign,false)
                },
                Err(why)=>{campaign.unsupported.insert(format!("fixture reachability not covered: {why}"));}
            }
        }else{security::challenges::generated_campaign(bound,&mut campaign,false);}
    }
    let sites=report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==security::Status::Unproved&&!campaign.violations.iter().any(|c|c.invariant_site==v.invariant.site.to_string()&&c.reachability.is_reachable())).map(|v|v.invariant.site.to_string()).collect();
    let campaign=security::challenges::run_selected_after(bound,Some(&sites),campaign);
    security::challenges::apply(&mut report,&campaign);
    if let Some(record)=cached {security::challenges::apply(&mut report,&security::challenges::Campaign{violations:record.violations,..Default::default()});}
    report
}
pub fn audit(options:&Options)->i32{
    let project=project_or_exit();
    let sources=match project.sources(){Ok(s)=>s,Err(e)=>{eprintln!("audit: {e}");return 2;}};
    let bound=compiled_or_exit(snapback4_lang::compile(&sources),options.json);
    // Audit is a permission map plus bounded evidence; `test` owns full campaigns.
    let report=report(&project,&bound,&sources,options);
    let dispositions=match super::security_reviews::review(&project,&sources,&report.notes,None){Ok(d)=>d,Err(error)=>{eprintln!("audit: E_SECURITY_NOTES: {error}");return 2;}};
    if options.json {let mut value=serde_json::to_value(&report).unwrap();value["securityReviews"]=serde_json::to_value(&dispositions).unwrap();println!("{value}");}
    else {print!("{}",report.text_with_all(options.flags.contains_key("all")));super::security_reviews::print(&dispositions);}
    if report.refuted(){1}else{0}
}
pub(super) fn exposure(report:&Report){
    let broad=report.exposures.iter().filter(|e|e.effects.get("read").is_some_and(|r|r=="allow"||r.starts_with("public"))).count();
    eprintln!("security exposure: {} tables, {} conditional audiences, {broad} broadly readable tables; run snapback4 audit for exact role/column predicates",report.exposures.len(),report.roles.len());
}
pub(super) fn summary(report:&Report,verbose:bool){
    let proved=report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==security::Status::Proved).count();
    let failures=report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==security::Status::Refuted&&v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|c|c.reachability.is_reachable())).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let refuted=report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==security::Status::Refuted).count();
    eprintln!("security: {proved} proved, {refuted} refuted, {} unproved ({} failing)",report.invariants.len()-proved-refuted,failures.len());
    for v in &failures {
        let c=v.counterexample.as_ref().unwrap();
        eprintln!("  FIX {}: {} via {} as {} ({}); tighten enforcement to the declared intent, then run snapback4 test",v.invariant.site,v.invariant.target_label(),c.operation,c.viewer,serde_json::to_value(&c.reachability).unwrap().as_str().unwrap());
    }
    let supplemental=report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==security::Status::Refuted&&v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|c|!c.reachability.is_reachable())).count();
    if supplemental>0 {eprintln!("  {supplemental} seed/synthetic observations (non-failing)");}
    if verbose {eprint!("{}",report.text_with_all(true));}
    else if !report.invariants.is_empty()||!report.campaign_coverage.is_empty(){eprintln!("  next: snapback4 test; {} coverage gaps (check --verbose/JSON keeps every reason)",report.campaign_coverage.len());}
    if !report.exposures.is_empty(){eprintln!("  review audiences and {} uncovered exposures: snapback4 audit",report.uncovered.len());}
}

/// A rule-changing preflight demands a current campaign, without pretending
/// finite tests or undeclared intent certify a deployment.
pub(super) fn release_loop(project:&Project,bound:&Bound,sources:&[(String,String)],prior:Option<&Bound>,options:&Options)->Result<Option<String>,String>{
    let changed=prior.is_none_or(|old|bound.schema.tables.iter().any(|(name,t)|old.schema.tables.get(name).is_none_or(|o|serde_json::to_value((&o.rules,&o.column_reads,&o.written_by)).ok()!=serde_json::to_value((&t.rules,&t.column_reads,&t.written_by)).ok()))||old.schema.tables.keys().any(|t|!bound.schema.tables.contains_key(t)));
    if !changed{return Ok(None);}
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.004#153-rule-changing-deployment-review — review is prominent, strictness is explicit and failure-origin aware.
    let report=report(project,bound,sources,options);
    let mut notice=String::from("SECURITY REVIEW — rules changed\n");
    for v in report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status==security::Status::Refuted&&v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|c|c.reachability.is_reachable())){
        let c=v.counterexample.as_ref().unwrap();
        notice.push_str(&format!("  FIX {} {}: refuted via {} as {} ({:?}); repair enforcement to match intent, then run snapback4 test\n",v.invariant.site,v.invariant.target_label(),c.operation,c.viewer,c.reachability));
    }
    for v in report.invariants.iter().filter(|v|v.status!=security::Status::Proved&&!v.counterexample.as_ref().is_some_and(|c|c.reachability.is_reachable())){
        notice.push_str(&format!("  REVIEW {} {}: unproved — {}; run snapback4 audit for all paths; preserve spec intent\n",v.invariant.site,v.invariant.target_label(),v.reasons.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("finite observations do not prove intent")));
    }
    for n in &report.notes{notice.push_str(&format!("  REVIEW {} {}: {}\n    {}\n",n.site,n.code,n.message,n.rewrite));}
    notice.push_str(&format!("  {}\n",release_notice(project,bound,sources,options)));
    notice.push_str(&format!("  {} independent invariants; {} coverage gaps; finite campaigns are not proof",bound.invariants.len(),report.campaign_coverage.len()));
    exposure(&report);eprintln!("{notice}");
    if options.flags.contains_key("strict")&&report.refuted(){return Err("E_SECURITY_REVIEW: --strict refuses reachable refuted security intent; repair the named rules and rerun snapback4 test before deploy".into());}
    Ok(Some(notice))
}
fn age(timestamp:Option<i64>,now:i64)->String{
    timestamp.map(|t|format!("at {t} ms since Unix epoch, age {}s",now.saturating_sub(t).max(0)/1000)).unwrap_or_else(||"time/age unknown (legacy record)".into())
}
fn release_notice(project:&Project,bound:&Bound,sources:&[(String,String)],options:&Options)->String{
    let selection=options.flags.get("schema").map(|s|format!(" --source {s:?}")).unwrap_or_default();
    let fixture=options.flags.get("fixture").map(|s|format!(" --fixture {s:?}")).unwrap_or_default();
    let now=snapback4_core::now_ms();
    let matching=record::matching(project,options,sources);
    let matches=matching.is_some();
    match matching.or_else(||record::latest(project)){
        Some(record)=>{
            let result=if !record.complete{"incomplete"}else if record.run_violations.unwrap_or(record.violations.len())>0{"FAILED"}else{"completed, no observed violation"};
            let current=if matches{"matches selected source/fixtures/CLI"}else{"STALE: source, fixtures or CLI differ; does not qualify selected release"};
            let next=if matches&&record.complete{"matching test campaign recorded (finite, not proof)".into()}else{format!("run `snapback4 test{selection}{fixture}` before deployment")};
            format!("last test: {result}, {}; {current}; {} retained reachable refutations, {} coverage gaps; last completed test {}; {next}",age(record.recorded_at,now),record.violations.len(),record.coverage_gaps,age(record.last_completed_at,now))
        },
        None=>format!("last test: NEVER RECORDED; run `snapback4 test{selection}{fixture}` before deployment; no matching completed campaign for this source, fixtures and CLI; {} independent invariants",bound.invariants.len()),
    }
}

//! Finite three-valued implication, deliberately independent of database facts.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#3-sound-proof-boundary — impossible valuations overapproximate all snapshots.
use snapback4_core::schema::{RuleExpr as R, RuleTerm as T};
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

pub const MAX_ATOMS: usize = 10;
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Truth { Yes, No, Unknown }
impl Truth {
    fn not(self) -> Self { match self { Self::Yes => Self::No, Self::No => Self::Yes, Self::Unknown => Self::Unknown } }
    fn combine(self, other: Self, and: bool) -> Self {
        let decisive = if and { Self::No } else { Self::Yes };
        if self == decisive || other == decisive { decisive }
        else if self == Self::Unknown || other == Self::Unknown { Self::Unknown }
        else { decisive.not() }
    }
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
enum Formula { Constant(Truth), Atom(usize), Not(Box<Self>), And(Vec<Self>), Or(Vec<Self>) }
impl Formula {
    fn eval(&self, values: &[Truth]) -> Truth {
        match self {
            Self::Constant(v) => *v, Self::Atom(n) => values[*n], Self::Not(x) => x.eval(values).not(),
            Self::And(xs) => xs.iter().fold(Truth::Yes, |v, x| v.combine(x.eval(values), true)),
            Self::Or(xs) => xs.iter().fold(Truth::No, |v, x| v.combine(x.eval(values), false)),
        }
    }
}
fn term(t: &T) -> T { match t { T::NextField(f) => T::Field(f.clone()), other => other.clone() } }
fn atom(rule: &R) -> String {
    let mut r = rule.clone();
    match &mut r {
        R::Eq(a,b) | R::Compare(_,a,b) => { *a=term(a); *b=term(b); }
        R::Exists { key, equalities, .. } | R::Created { key, equalities, .. } => {
            for t in key { *t=term(t); }
            for (_,t) in equalities.iter_mut() { *t=term(t); }
            equalities.sort_by(|a,b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
        }
        _ => {}
    }
    if let R::Eq(a,b)=&mut r && serde_json::to_string(a).unwrap()>serde_json::to_string(b).unwrap() { std::mem::swap(a,b); }
    let mut json=serde_json::to_value(&r).unwrap();
    // Provenance controls planning, not rule evaluation. Remove only this
    // leaf's metadata, never a similarly named literal-object field.
    for name in ["Exists","Created"] { if let Some(body)=json.get_mut(name).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_object_mut) { body.remove("provenance"); } }
    json.to_string()
}
fn formula(rule: &R, atoms: &mut Vec<String>, nodes: &mut usize) -> Result<Formula, String> {
    *nodes+=1; if *nodes>1024 { return Err("formula exceeds 1024 nodes".into()); }
    Ok(match rule {
        R::Allow | R::Public {..} => Formula::Constant(Truth::Yes), R::Deny => Formula::Constant(Truth::No),
        R::And(xs) => Formula::And(xs.iter().map(|r| formula(r,atoms,nodes)).collect::<Result<_,_>>()?),
        R::Or(xs) => Formula::Or(xs.iter().map(|r| formula(r,atoms,nodes)).collect::<Result<_,_>>()?),
        R::Not(x) => Formula::Not(Box::new(formula(x,atoms,nodes)?)),
        R::Ne(a,b) => Formula::Not(Box::new(formula(&R::Eq(a.clone(),b.clone()),atoms,nodes)?)),
        R::Eq(T::Literal(a),T::Literal(b)) => Formula::Constant(if a==b {Truth::Yes}else{Truth::No}),
        R::Eq(T::Viewer,T::Viewer) => Formula::Constant(Truth::Yes),
        other => { let key=atom(other); let n=atoms.iter().position(|a| a==&key).unwrap_or_else(|| {atoms.push(key);atoms.len()-1});
            if atoms.len()>MAX_ATOMS {return Err(format!("more than {MAX_ATOMS} independent predicates"));} Formula::Atom(n) }
    })
}
// @ref LLP 3000.036.004#133-coverage-and-bounded-checking — exact inputs only; no fixture assumptions.
thread_local! {
    static IMPLICATIONS: std::cell::RefCell<std::collections::BTreeMap<String,Result<bool,String>>> = const { std::cell::RefCell::new(std::collections::BTreeMap::new()) };
}
/// Only exact kernel implication results are reused, never concrete judgments.
pub fn implies(admission: &R, policy: &R) -> Result<bool,String> {
    let key=serde_json::to_string(&(admission,policy)).unwrap();
    if let Some(result)=IMPLICATIONS.with(|cache|cache.borrow().get(&key).cloned()){return result;}
    let result=uncached(admission,policy);
    IMPLICATIONS.with(|cache|{let mut cache=cache.borrow_mut();if cache.len()>=4096{cache.clear();}cache.insert(key,result.clone());});
    result
}
fn uncached(admission: &R, policy: &R) -> Result<bool,String> {
    let (mut atoms,mut nodes)=(Vec::new(),0);
    let a=formula(admission,&mut atoms,&mut nodes)?;
    let p=formula(policy,&mut atoms,&mut nodes)?;
    let mut values=vec![Truth::Unknown;atoms.len()];
    for mut n in 0..3usize.pow(atoms.len() as u32) {
        for v in &mut values { *v=match n%3 {0=>Truth::Yes,1=>Truth::No,_=>Truth::Unknown}; n/=3; }
        if a.eval(&values)==Truth::Yes && p.eval(&values)!=Truth::Yes { return Ok(false); }
    }
    Ok(true)
}
pub fn dependencies(rule: &R) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut out=BTreeSet::new();
    match rule {
        R::Exists{table,key,equalities,..}|R::Created{table,key,equalities,..} => {out.insert(table.clone());for term in key.iter().chain(equalities.iter().map(|(_,t)|t)){for (table,_) in term.references(){out.insert(table.into());}}}
        R::And(xs)|R::Or(xs) => for x in xs {out.extend(dependencies(x));}, R::Not(x) => out.extend(dependencies(x)),
        R::Eq(a,b)|R::Ne(a,b)|R::Compare(_,a,b) => for t in [a,b] { for (table,_) in t.references() {out.insert(table.into());} },
        _=>{}
    }
    out
}

pub fn bind_rule(catalog: &Catalog, info: &TableInfo, rule: &RuleDecl) -> Fallible<RuleExpr> {
    let bindings = RuleBindings { old: rule.bindings.first().cloned(), next: rule.bindings.get(1).cloned(), update: rule.effect == Effect::Update, insert: rule.effect == Effect::Insert, hops: rule.effect != Effect::Read, present: Vec::new() };
    rule_expr(catalog, info, &rule.value, &bindings).map_err(|error| {
        let mut error = super::first_paste::inherited_rule(catalog, info, rule).unwrap_or(error);
        if error.code == "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR" && rule.effect == Effect::Update && rule.bindings.is_empty()
            && error.rewrite == "write this as a named transition" {
            let source = super::rule_operator::named_update_source(&rule.value);
            error.rewrite = format!("name both row images: `{source}`");
            error.source_rewrite = Some(source);
            error.source_rewrite_kind = Some(crate::diag::SourceRewriteKind::NamedUpdate);
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.6 — the named form of a whole unnamed update rule, so the rewrite keeps every other clause.
        if error.code == "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR" && rule.effect == Effect::Update && rule.bindings.is_empty() && error.rewrite.starts_with("name both images") {
            let comparison = error.message.split('`').nth(1).unwrap_or_default().to_owned();
            error.rewrite = super::rule_operator::named_update(&info.decl.name, &rule.value, &comparison);
        }
        if error.code == "E_QUARRY_RULE_HOP" {
            error.rewrite = match rule.effect {
                Effect::Read => reference::read_hop_rewrite(catalog, info, &rule.value).unwrap_or_else(|| "a read rule probes one hop: copy the deciding value onto this row (immutable, checked against the parent by the insert rule), or use read through .parent".into()),
                _ => reference::reference_rewrite(catalog, info, &rule.value),
            };
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.036#14.3 — a read-through child binds its parent's rule over hidden
        // captures (`.$enrollment.dancer`): its refusal is the parent's (`internal_names` drops the copy).
        // @ref LLP 3000.036#15.6 — a `read through` that did not expand (E_READ_THROUGH says why)
        // leaves its internal call; its refusal is that problem's cascade, spelled as written.
        if let Expr::Call { name, args, .. } = &rule.value && matches!(name.as_str(), "$readThrough" | "$readThroughLive") {
            let reference = match args.as_slice() { [Expr::Name { name, .. }] => name.clone(), _ => "parent".into() };
            error.message = format!("`read through .{reference}` did not expand, so {} has no read rule yet", info.decl.name);
            // The cascade convention: `check` hides it beside its cause unless --verbose.
            error.rewrite = "fix this Quarry line and rerun snapback4 check".into();
            error.cascade_of = Some(rule.site.clone());
            error.mechanical = false;
            return error;
        }
        if rule.effect == Effect::Read && let Some(through) = &info.through {
            error.rewrite = format!("repair {}'s read rule (its own diagnostic prints the repair); {} reads through it", through.parent, info.decl.name);
            error.cascade_of = Some(error.site.clone());
        }
        error
    })
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct RuleBindings {
    old: Option<String>,
    next: Option<String>,
    update: bool,
    insert: bool,
    hops: bool,
    present: Vec<RuleTerm>,
}

// @ref LLP 3000.013#2.2 — presence facts retain a reference term's old/next image.
// Facts hold on the logical edge where the next operand can affect truth.
// Expiry accounting may evaluate other edges too: the shared runtime returns
// no witness for an ordinary unique null key, without accessing tied rows.
// Thus admission does not require physical short-circuiting. Facts still
// cannot leak from one OR alternative into an unrelated alternative.
fn present_terms(rule: &RuleExpr, truth: bool) -> Vec<RuleTerm> {
        },
        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } if op == "not" => Ok(RuleExpr::Not(Box::new(rule_expr(catalog, info, value, bindings)?))),
        Expr::Member { .. } => {
            let (term, ty) = rule_term(catalog,info,expr,bindings)?;
            if ty != Ty::Bool { return Err(type_error(site,"a bare rule field must be bool","compare this field with a value of its declared type")); }
            Ok(RuleExpr::Eq(term,RuleTerm::Literal(Value::Bool(true))))
        }
        Expr::Exists { read, site } => {
            let (table, index, key, equalities) = probe(catalog, info, read, site, bindings, true).map_err(|error| super::bracket_ranges::refusal(read, true, error))?;
            Ok(RuleExpr::Exists { table, index, key, equalities, provenance: KeyProvenance::Shape })
        }
        Expr::Created { read, site } => {
            if !bindings.insert {
                return Err(unknown(site, "created is valid only in an insert rule", "use exists in read, update and delete rules"));
            }
            let (table, index, key, equalities) = probe(catalog, info, read, site, bindings, true)?;
            Ok(RuleExpr::Created { table, index, key, equalities, provenance: KeyProvenance::Shape })
        }
        Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(b), .. } => Ok(if *b { RuleExpr::Allow } else { RuleExpr::Deny }),
        Expr::Call { .. } => {
            let effect = super::rule_operator::effect_word(bindings.insert, bindings.update, !bindings.hops);
            Err(super::rule_operator::diagnostic(site, &info.decl.name, effect, bindings.update && bindings.old.is_some(), expr, "a helper or function call"))
        }
        other => Err(unknown(site, format!("`{}` is not a rule", crate::print::expression(other)), "read <- exists memberships[.conversationId, viewer]")),
    }
}

## 16. SEC7: advice that reaches the builder

Implementer: Codex for Charlie Cheever, 2026-10-22. Wave-22 commission;
DX6 owns session/upgrade/clock and frontend/proof-kit fixes. No version bump.
This section supersedes §15.2's special display cap for insert/result notes and
§12.3's advisory-only boundary only for the two explicit gates below.
It also revises §§13.5/14.2/14.5/14.6: disposition-clearable review gates are
a new exit-1 category alongside replayed intent violations, including without
invariants. Their zero-new-refusal bars continue to bind failures no disposition
can clear (compilation failures and reachable refutations). Gate counts and
legitimate review costs are reported separately, never called replayed exploits. Runtime
authority and the proved/refuted/unproved contract remain unchanged.

### 16.1 Presentation and conditional questions

A shared severity ordering puts gated notes and likely-hole questions before
coverage, restates and result inventories. Default check retains every priority
0–2 likely-hole question and the first five ordinary code classes in severity
order, keeping each selected class's distinct sites/audiences; SEC6 insert/result
notes never increase that budget. Result exposure notes group by source table, retaining every operation,
column, observer kind and source site in JSON/full text. Audit uses the same
severity and numeric file/line/column ordering, never lexicographic site strings.
Insert-write advice requires an explicitly supplied nonliteral expression whose
flow uses a mutation argument; omitted defaults and literal-only assignments are
quiet. These are precision changes to advice, never creation-policy inference.

New advisory classes ask about: reason text without a positive non-whitespace
minimum; optional money supplied to creation; constant true payment/approval
flags (a naming heuristic, explicitly a question); competing generic enum setters
versus stricter literal transitions; mutable creation checks omitted by a later
transition or derived creation; inconsistent server-now duration bounds on the
same bound column across operations; and global-role operations recording viewer
on an unrelated row. Restating questions and the draft ask whether each role may
write any row, independently of the read questionnaire. The relationship recipe
models the owner of this wall explicitly. These shapes cannot infer the spec.

### 16.2 Narrow gates and individual dispositions

N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE: an optional image/file mutation argument flows to an
insert/upsert of a media column, including a conditional child insertion. A
non-null guard around just the child does not establish required parent evidence.
An unconditional dominating require of non-null before any creating write can
exclude the note; aliases/helpers are resolved by the existing authority walker.
Optionality may be intentional: the gate requires review, never asserts an exploit.

N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT: a read branch trusts a retained grant; an authored grant
writer requires a literal role on the principal argument stored as that grant's
reader principal; that role is mutable through authored operations; and the read
branch does not imply the same current-reader role. Require a positive recipient
role atom in every admitting writer branch; do not mistake the assigner's role
for the recipient's. The gate excludes ordinary owner branches, literal service
seats and mere caller-role requirements. Revoking derived grants is a repair;
static inability to prove full revocation remains reviewable, not an automatic
safety theorem. General N_GRANT_OUTLIVES_ROLE stays advisory.

Unreviewed gates make check exit 1 with structured note IDs, without marking an
invariant refuted. The existing bulk --ack-notes cannot clear a security gate.
Use check --ack-security <id> --reason '<spec rationale>' for one current note.
Store versioned dispositions in snapback/security-reviews.json with ID, reason,
source digest and analyzer revision. IDs hash the complete diagnostic; the source
digest hashes all compiled source filenames and bytes in sorted order. Every
source edit, changed diagnostic or analyzer revision invalidates the disposition.
Blank reasons, unknown IDs, malformed files and incompatible flag combinations
refuse. Writes use temp+rename and verify compiled sources still match disk;
failed compilation/refuted intent must never record acknowledgments. Dispositions
are review records, never authority or proof, remain visible in JSON/audit and
can be checked into source control. Broad advice may also be individually reviewed.

### 16.3 Directed finite histories

Keep the 512 breadth/pair budget. Add a separate bounded directed frontier before
breadth exploration for schema enum transitions and mutable dependencies of
independent intent/creator checks. Generate successors from the current world,
so references returned/created at one step are available later. Track semantic
state signatures over status/role/boolean/relationship fields, rather than minted
IDs alone; prioritize unseen lifecycle signatures and schema-relevant mutations.
Bound depth to eight authored mutations, attempts to 2048 and retained frontier
to 16 worlds; share check's existing work/deadline cap and report every cut.
Actual mutation admission, executed-write judgments and ordinary observers remain
the only failure oracle. Synthetic witnesses remain REVIEW and never failures.
Validated generated initial fixtures retain their explicit provenance. No seed
state is relabeled application reachable, and finite exhaustion remains unproved.

### 16.4 Qualification

Regression tests cover positive and negative shapes, helper/alias guards,
            if histories::violation(out,inv,steps,viewer,row,None,initial,"mutation result"){
                let v=out.violations.last_mut().unwrap();v.operation=p.name.clone();v.args=steps.last().map(|s|s.args.clone()).unwrap_or_default();v.rule_path="authored mutation returned a compiler-typed protected row/column payload; stable current policy false".into();
            }
        }
    }
}

// Follow an actually admitted state change with payload-bearing operations on
// the same referenced row. This finds lifecycle-to-mutation observations without
// spending pair slots on unrelated roster and creation combinations.
pub(super) fn pairs(bound:&Bound,candidates:&[(&Program,String,BTreeMap<String,Value>)],committed:&[usize])->Vec<(usize,usize)>{
    let protected=bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|i.target=="read").map(|i|i.table.clone()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
    let mut groups:BTreeMap<(String,String),Vec<(usize,usize)>>=BTreeMap::new();let mut seen=BTreeSet::new();
    for (second,(p,actor,args)) in candidates.iter().enumerate(){
        let Some(bp)=bound.programs.iter().find(|bp|bp.program.name==p.name)else{continue;};
        for &first in committed{
            let (before,who,inputs)=&candidates[first];if before.name==p.name{continue;}
            let shared=protected.iter().any(|table|histories::typed_source(&bp.result,table)&&ir::write_tables(before).iter().any(|(t,_)|t==table)&&before.args.iter().any(|(a,k)|matches!(k,ir::ArgType::Ref{table:t} if t==table)&&p.args.iter().any(|(b,k)|matches!(k,ir::ArgType::Ref{table:t} if t==table)&&inputs.get(a)==args.get(b))));
            if shared&&seen.insert((before.name.clone(),who.clone(),p.name.clone(),actor.clone())){groups.entry((p.name.clone(),actor.clone())).or_default().push((first,second));}
        }
    }
    let mut out=Vec::new();for n in 0..groups.values().map(Vec::len).max().unwrap_or(0){for group in groups.values(){if let Some(pair)=group.get(n){out.push(*pair);if out.len()==256{return out;}}}}out
}

// Identify direct argument supplies to declared column-write intent. This only
// prioritizes proposals; actual interpreter admission still decides every case.
pub(super) fn write_arguments(bound:&Bound,p:&Program)->BTreeSet<String>{
    fn walk(v:&serde_json::Value,f:&mut impl FnMut(&serde_json::Value)){
        f(v);match v{serde_json::Value::Object(xs)=>for x in xs.values(){walk(x,f)},serde_json::Value::Array(xs)=>for x in xs{walk(x,f)},_=>{}}
    }
    let json=serde_json::to_value(p).unwrap();let mut bindings=BTreeMap::new();
    walk(&json,&mut |v|for tag in ["Const","Let"]{if let Some(b)=v.get(tag)&&let(Some(n),Some(e))=(b.get("name").and_then(|v|v.as_str()),b.get("value")){bindings.insert(n.to_string(),e.clone());}});
    fn resolve<'a>(v:&'a serde_json::Value,bindings:&'a BTreeMap<String,serde_json::Value>,depth:usize)->&'a serde_json::Value{
        if depth>32{return v;}if let Some(n)=v.get("Variable").and_then(|v|v.as_str())&&let Some(e)=bindings.get(n){resolve(e,bindings,depth+1)}else{v}
    }
    let mut out=BTreeSet::new();
    walk(&json,&mut |v|for tag in ["Insert","InsertIfAbsent","Upsert","Update","WriteTarget"]{
        let Some(w)=v.get(tag)else{continue;};let table=w.get("table").or_else(||w.get("target").and_then(|t|t.get("table"))).and_then(|v|v.as_str());
        let Some(payload)=w.get("row").or_else(||w.get("patch"))else{continue;};let payload=resolve(payload,&bindings,0);
        let Some(fields)=payload.get("Object").and_then(|v|v.as_object())else{continue;};
        for inv in bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|Some(i.table.as_str())==table&&i.column.is_some()&&!matches!(i.target.as_str(),"read"|"always")&&i.operation.as_ref().is_none_or(|op|op==&p.name)){
            if let Some(value)=fields.get(inv.column.as_ref().unwrap())&&let Some(arg)=resolve(value,&bindings,0).get("Variable").and_then(|v|v.as_str())&&p.args.contains_key(arg){out.insert(arg.into());}
        }
    });out
}
    let payload=|data:&Value|matches!(data,Value::Row(_))&&data.field("id").ok()==Some(key)&&column.is_none_or(|c|data.field(c).ok().is_some_and(|v|physical.field(c).ok()==Some(v)))&&policy.is_none_or(|p|!p.any_term(&|term|{
        let column=match term{RuleTerm::Field(c)|RuleTerm::OldField(c)|RuleTerm::NextField(c)=>Some(c.as_str()),RuleTerm::Reference{column,..}|RuleTerm::ReferenceChain{column,..}=>Some(column.as_str()),_=>None};
        column.filter(|c|*c!="$security:server-clock").is_some_and(|c|data.field(c).is_err()||data.field(c).ok()!=physical.field(c).ok())
    }));
    match ty{
        Ty::Row(t)|Ty::WriteRow(t) if t==table=>payload(data),
        Ty::Optional(inner)|Ty::Omittable(inner)=>typed_disclosure_image(inner,data,table,key,column,physical,policy),
        Ty::Page(t,_) if t==table=>matches!(data,Value::Array(xs) if xs.iter().any(payload)),
        Ty::List(inner,_)|Ty::Collection(inner,_)=>matches!(data,Value::Array(xs) if xs.iter().any(|r|typed_disclosure_image(inner,r,table,key,column,physical,policy))),
        Ty::Object(fields)|Ty::RowShape(fields)|Ty::RowObject(fields)=>fields.iter().any(|(name,ty)|data.field(name).ok().is_some_and(|v|typed_disclosure_image(ty,v,table,key,column,physical,policy))),
        _=>false,
    }
}
pub(super) fn typed_source(ty:&crate::types::Ty,table:&str)->bool{
    use crate::types::Ty;
    match ty{Ty::Row(t)|Ty::WriteRow(t)|Ty::Page(t,_)=>t==table,Ty::Optional(inner)|Ty::Omittable(inner)|Ty::List(inner,_)|Ty::Collection(inner,_)=>typed_source(inner,table),Ty::Object(fields)|Ty::RowShape(fields)|Ty::RowObject(fields)=>fields.values().any(|ty|typed_source(ty,table)),_=>false}
}
pub(super) fn observer_tables(bound:&Bound,table:&str)->BTreeSet<String>{
    let mut out=BTreeSet::from([table.into()]);
    loop{let before=out.len();
        for m in &bound.schema.maintains{if out.contains(&m.source){out.insert(m.target.clone());if let Some(owner)=&m.private{out.insert(owner.table.clone());}}}
        for (name,t) in &bound.schema.tables{if t.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|edge|out.contains(&edge.parent))||super::super::columns::rules(t).any(|r|kernel::dependencies(r).iter().any(|t|out.contains(t))){out.insert(name.clone());}}
        if out.len()==before{return out;}
    }
}
fn reserve_observers(out:&mut Campaign,calls:usize)->bool{
    if !out.reserve(calls){return false;}
    if out.history_observer_calls+calls>32768{out.unsupported.insert("history read observers capped at 32768 calls; remaining disclosure combinations not covered".into());false}else{out.history_observer_calls+=calls;true}
}
fn observe(bound:&Bound,e:&mut Engine,rows:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,initial:&BTreeMap<String,Vec<Value>>,actors:&[String],steps:&[Step],out:&mut Campaign){
    if !reserve_observers(out,0)||out.history_observer_calls>=32768{return;}
    let queries=bound.programs.iter().filter(|bp|bp.program.kind==ProgramKind::Query&&!bp.program.native).filter(|bp|{
        let json=serde_json::to_string(&bp.program).unwrap();
        if ["NewId","Emit","JobAs","JobQuery"].iter().any(|tag|json.contains(tag)){
            out.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: generated-id/opaque history observer needs disclosure provenance",bp.program.name));false
        }else{true}
    }).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    if queries.is_empty(){return;}
    for inv in bound.invariants.iter().filter(|i|i.target=="read"){
        let direct=inv.policy.as_ref().is_some_and(|p|kernel::implies(&super::super::columns::admission(&bound.schema.tables[&inv.table],inv.column.as_deref()),p)==Ok(true));
        let indirect=bound.schema.maintains.iter().any(|m|m.source==inv.table)||bound.schema.tables.values().any(|t|super::super::columns::rules(t).any(|r|kernel::dependencies(r).contains(&inv.table)));
        if direct&&!indirect{continue;}

        let observing=observer_tables(bound,&inv.table);
        for row in rows.get(&inv.table).into_iter().flatten(){'actors:for viewer in actors{
            if out.exhausted(){return;}
            if out.violations.iter().any(|v|v.invariant_site==inv.site.to_string()&&v.viewer==*viewer&&v.reachability==Reachability::AuthoredFixtureTrace&&trace_key(&v.history)==trace_key(steps)){continue;}
            if !reserve_observers(out,1){return;}
            match policy_in(bound,inv,rows,viewer,None,row,e){Ok(false)=>{},Ok(true)=>continue,Err(why)=>{out.unsupported.insert(format!("{}: {why}",inv.target_label()));continue;}}
            let Ok(key)=row.field("id")else{continue;};
            if inv.column.as_ref().and_then(|c|bound.schema.tables[&inv.table].written_by.get(c)).is_some_and(|gate|!gate.audience&&row.field(&gate.owner).ok()!=Some(&Value::Id(viewer.clone()))){continue 'actors;}

            // A typed authored row return is already a payload witness. It does
