//! Quarry for Snapback 4: one language for tables, rules and programs
//! (LLP 2000.000 §5.1), bound to the core IR in Rust so `check` runs in
//! milliseconds with no other runtime.

pub mod ast;
pub mod bind;
pub mod diag;
pub mod emit;
pub mod guide;
pub mod lexer;
pub mod parser;
pub mod print;
pub mod source;
pub mod recipe;
mod repair;
pub mod types;
pub mod release_changes;
pub mod client_contracts;
mod result_domains;

pub use bind::{Bound, BoundProgram, bind};
pub use bind::security;
pub use diag::{Diagnostic, Site};
pub use parser::parse_document;

/// Parse and bind a set of `(file name, source)` documents.
pub fn compile(sources: &[(String, String)]) -> Bound {
    let mut documents = Vec::new();
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    for (file, source) in sources {
        let (document, mut parsed) = parse_document(file, source);
        diagnostics.append(&mut parsed);
        documents.push(document);
    }
    // Refusals still block binding. On these malformed forms only, complete
    // their repairs with column types/table names from the whole project,
    // including files and declarations that follow the offending operation.
    let repair_files: std::collections::BTreeSet<_> = diagnostics.iter().filter(|d|
        d.code == "E_QUARRY_SELF_EQUALITY" || (d.code == "E_QUARRY_UNSUPPORTED" && d.message.starts_with("count(*)")))
        .map(|d| d.site.file.clone()).collect();
    if !repair_files.is_empty() {
        let tables: Vec<_> = documents.iter().flat_map(|doc| doc.tables.iter().cloned()).collect();
        // Use the ordinary binder's projected types, including renamed and
        // computed fields. Invalid or non-scalar projections get no invented
        // argument type. This discarded binding is diagnostic-only.
        let views = if documents.iter().any(|doc| !doc.views.is_empty() || !doc.feed_views.is_empty()) {
            let mut declarations = documents.clone();
            for doc in &mut declarations {
                doc.programs.clear(); doc.actions.clear(); doc.routes.clear(); doc.schedules.clear();
            }
            bind(declarations).view_types
        } else { Default::default() };
        diagnostics.retain(|d| !repair_files.contains(&d.site.file));
        for ((file, source), document) in sources.iter().zip(&mut documents) {
            if repair_files.contains(file) {
                let (repaired, mut parsed) = parser::parse_with_types(file, source, tables.clone(), views.clone());
                *document = repaired;
                diagnostics.append(&mut parsed);
            }
        }
    }
    bind::audience_diagnostics::parser_context(&documents, &mut diagnostics);
    repair::verify(&documents, &mut diagnostics);
    if !diagnostics.is_empty() {
        return Bound { invariants: Vec::new(), receipt_members: Default::default(), refusal_sites: Default::default(), view_types: Default::default(), server: documents.iter().any(|doc| doc.server), schema: Default::default(), programs: Vec::new(), personas: Vec::new(), diagnostics, notes: Vec::new() };
    }

# Security invariants

State privacy intent separately from enforcement. Check reports proved, refuted
with a replayed counterexample, or unproved with a reason; passing finite tests
are not proofs.

```quarry
table privateNotes:
  patient: principal
  body: text 1..2000
  sealed: bool default false
  read <- .patient = viewer and .sealed = false
  insert <- .patient = viewer and .sealed = false
  online only
-- Spec: a patient may see only their own note; sealing may narrow availability.
-- Removing an accidental broad branch from the rule must not change this intent.
invariant privateNotes.read only .patient = viewer
invariant privateNotes.body read only .patient = viewer
invariant privateNotes.insert only .patient = viewer
query privateNote(note: privateNotes):
  return privateNotes[note]
mutation writePrivateNote(body: text 1..2000):
  return insert privateNotes { patient: viewer, body }
```

## Reference

`invariant table.column read only P` protects a column value, derived values and value-dependent counts/existence/refusals. Mutation results, implicit final writes and explicit returned row objects are observers too. A query projection alone is not privacy: use column read rules to protect every operation. An authored projection excluding the column does not by itself disclose that value; filtering, ordering or copying it can. Audit JSON includes `column_audiences` (effective row rule plus private-owner gate). Unknown derived and opaque paths remain unproved.

`invariant table.read only P` protects read intent; insert, update and delete
name authority. `invariant table.column write only P` covers writes to a
column (insert, inserted insert-if-absent, update and both upsert arms).
Creation is not exempt from write intent; tests judge each executed write in
a committed mutation, including intermediate writes in a multi-write operation. `invariant table.column update only P` checks
only edits, retaining old-and-next-image semantics; use it when creation is permitted
to a different role (for example counter staff creating a ticket price). `invariant table always P` states row integrity.
An update policy over `.field` constrains **both old and next images**.
A policy saying status must not be override therefore also restricts editing
a row that was already override, even when changing it away from that status.
For the role authority of one named mutation, use operation-specific intent
(`invariant table.operation only P`) instead. General next-image-only and
cross-operation transition assertions still need a separate reduction.
Predicates use the existing rule vocabulary: `.field`, `viewer`, `exists`,
comparisons, `and`, `or`, `not`. For a role write use the complete roster probe,
for example `invariant members.role write only exists roles[viewer, role = 'owner']`
in a schema declaring those tables. A declaration never grants authority. Whole-row read intent also protects logical
existence: when occupancy totals are intentionally public but roster identities
are private, declare column read intent for those identities instead. Include
a service seat explicitly when the spec permits it; seats are ordinary checked
viewers, never implicitly exempt.

The implemented proof fragment exhaustively checks independent three-valued
rule predicates. A failed implication is unproved until an engine replay
establishes a counterexample. A schema-valid seeded snapshot is not a claim
that an application operation sequence reaches that state. Required-column
non-null assertions have a separate validation theorem. Read/count/sum/existence obligations are reported separately. A maintained aggregate with bare privacy keys can prove its contributor audience; a broader aggregate can yield a paired present/absent counterexample. Exact server `not before`/`expire at` bounds can prove a temporal read component independently of physical sweeps. General transitions and unsupported expressions remain unproved.
Read-through captures/live parents, complex derived aggregates, raw rule probes,
owned-field update bypasses, cascade/set-null and opaque jobs/workers need
separate reductions. An unresolved path blocks the whole declaration's proof.

Server delivery authorizes against the current server snapshot. A disconnected
device can retain an earlier snapshot until it receives a revocation; even
`until-revoked` cannot know a later server role. Synced current-role intent is
therefore unproved for device access. Retained history follows its leave policy.
These reports exclude physical timing and resource/meter side channels and
explicitly exclude the trusted system-principal boundary. Service seats remain
inside the ordinary-viewer check; there is no implicit seat exemption.

## Current roles and derived grants

A membership or assignment created while a user is an inspector can survive
their demotion. Conjoin the **current reader's role** with the assignment
branch, or revoke every derived grant transactionally whenever the role changes.
A grant writer's role does not establish the recipient's current authority.
With independent current-role intent, grant-lifetime advice points at this pattern; the argument-grant advice identifies
arguments written into reader-grant columns: validate the chosen principal's
role and relationship, even when the caller is privileged.
Global admin authority must come from a trusted operator or existing admin;
a group-creation `created` probe must remain scoped to that group everywhere.
`N_PRIVILEGE_ESCALATION` identifies role assignments trusted by later rules without independent delegation. Open enrollment may be intentional: compare each note with the specification. See `guide staging` for operator first-admin setup and `guide sharing` for parent authority.

## Required evidence and deadlines

If the spec requires a photo, use a required `image <=5000000` column or
`[image <=5000000] 1..4`; `?` permits omission and `[image] <=4` permits zero.
Uploads are verified media and asset reads inherit row and private-field rules.
Optional-evidence advice asks the builder to check intentional optionality.
Text `min..max` counts non-whitespace Unicode characters toward the minimum;
the maximum counts all characters. Stored text is not trimmed or rewritten.
A sweep changes state eventually: compare the deadline with server `now` in
the mutation too if writes must stop exactly at that instant.

## Existence observations

A lookup that says NOT_FOUND on absence followed by a denial saying FORBIDDEN
can reveal existence to callers admitted by a broader read rule. Use the same
code **and message** for hidden/absent/denied cases when existence is private,
or tighten the table read rule. Program `exists` is caller-filtered; probes
inside table rules inspect raw rows and can disclose predicates indirectly.
Inspect both paths in `audit`; a payload-only read check is insufficient.

## When an observer remains unproved

The report names the edge that lacks a reduction. Preserve the specification
while changing its enforcement; weakening an invariant to match a leaking
rule does not repair privacy.

- Maintained counts/sums: retain privacy fields as ordinary bare group keys
  and protect the aggregate with the same audience predicate. Recorded
  reference paths, calendar keys, derived values, private columns and temporal
  contributors need their own reduction; their names are not source fields.
- Owner fields: declare column-write intent too. `written by` authorizes
  patches even when the ordinary update rule denies. To prove a particular
  mutation's role authority, use a dominating current-role requirement and
  operation-specific intent over a role table the mutation cannot change.
  This does not prove every owner-field or old/next-image path.
- Raw rule probes: inspect the observing table and its writers. A protected
  target's read rule does not protect predicates probed from another rule.
  Apply the intended audience at that observer, or remove the raw dependency;
  the report retains the unsupported edge until it can establish implication.
- Cascade/set-null: automatic child changes bypass child write rules. An
  explicit authorized child mutation with `restrict` removes that automatic
  writer, but parent refusal/existence and transitive references remain
  separate observations. Read-through/live-parent authority requires a separate reduction.
- Jobs/native workers/actions: the audit names the trusted or opaque writer.
  An ordinary mutation with stable role requirements can prove that mutation's
  authority; arbitrary native/worker output cannot acquire a proof from a
  caller's role or a passing finite test.
- Schedules: use a stored `not before`/`expire at` lifetime for exact read
  boundaries, or compare server `now` in the write itself. A scheduled status
  update leaves the old status visible between deadline and sweep.

Default `test` challenges pure-schema applications through a private production
`serve`: unauthenticated calls, forged persona headers and development doors.
The host uses no pre-existing developer credentials or development mode. Applications needing
native/worker artifacts are explicitly not covered by that schema-only host.
Focused fixtures also enable short ordered mutation histories followed by
ordinary reads; traces record actual calls and current policy evaluation.
Named personas/service seats and enum argument combinations are enumerated
within reported limits. Asset challenges use real foreign-upload and verified
non-image ledgers; video arguments and unvisited histories remain named. Complete fixture stores preserve image/file ledgers, captures, read-through deadlines, maintained views and expiry. Histories include fixture principals and reference-row candidates, under a reported work cap. Neither
these finite campaigns nor an offline device's retained snapshot establishes

E_SECURITY_REVIEW means strict rule-changing deployment refused because reachable
security intent is refuted. Repair enforcement to match independent intent and
rerun test for the selected source and fixtures. Unproved notes and synthetic-only
observations do not cause this refusal.

### E_SESSION

E_SESSION means a supplied client session is malformed. Pass the complete Session
returned by guest, login, signup or your service, including principal, kind, token
and positive integer expiresAt milliseconds; the online token option accepts a bare
bearer. Constructors refuse before transport, storage, device or timer work.
Shape validation grants no authority; the server still decides session validity.

## Individual security review

Default check puts likely holes before result inventories and restating questions.
Questions about retained role grants and uploads with an explicit mandatory-media
contract require a repair or an individual disposition. They fail check without claiming an invariant refutation.
Read the note, compare it with the specification, then use
`check --ack-security ID --reason 'specification rationale'` with its current ID
from check or check --json. Bulk --ack-notes cannot clear these gates.
Commit snapback/security-reviews.json when the decision should travel with source.
Every Quarry edit, changed diagnostic or security analyzer revision requires review
again; the record never grants authority or proves safety. Audit retains the full
notes and dispositions. Declared refutations still fail and cannot be acknowledged.
Deploy --strict retains its refutation gate; run check in acceptance before deploy.

Optional arguments and optional columns are valid, including deliberate loosening.
A required child media column validates an existing attachment; it does not require
a child row. Guarded optional attachments need no acknowledgment. When independent
parent integrity intent requires a child, require evidence before creating that
parent. Without such intent, a conditional child is an advisory spec question. Reasons use text 1..N when nonempty justification is required; optional
money and constant payment/approval flags need independent specification review.
Transition advice asks whether a generic setter can bypass a stricter decision or
whether eligibility checked at creation must be rechecked at approval. Different
duration windows on one column may be deliberate: confirm them against the spec.
Role-wide write questions ask whether a global role may write every resource.
Model the owner of this particular wall; see `guide rule-recipes --section "Wall ownership"`.

Test explores directed status/eligibility histories up to eight mutations with a
separate finite successor bound. Check keeps its shared 512-work/1500ms limit.
Frontier, argument, signature and attempt cuts remain coverage gaps. Synthetic
observations are REVIEW, while actual admitted histories from validated generated
fixtures retain their generated-fixture-trace origin and can fail acceptance.

### N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT

N_RETAINED_ROLE_GRANT: A recipient role required when storing a grant is mutable and missing from a reader branch that trusts that grant, including column payload readers. Recheck current role or revoke derived grants. Intentional retained authority needs an individual source-bound disposition.

### N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE

N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE: An optional upload argument can be omitted despite a required media column or explicit non-null integrity intent. Require the upload before creating the parent when independent intent requires child evidence. Optional media columns and guarded optional attachments do not require acknowledgment; a required child column alone does not require a child row. Review an intentional exception with an individual source-bound disposition.

### N_CREATION_REASON

N_CREATION_REASON: Creating a row accepts a reason argument without a positive non-whitespace minimum. Compare the justification requirement with the spec; use text 1..N when required. This name-based question is advisory.

### N_CREATION_MONEY

N_CREATION_MONEY: Creating a row accepts omitted money. Model and require the amount when the spec requires a fee or payment; confirm intentional optional amounts against the spec. This name-based question is advisory.

### N_CONSTANT_APPROVAL

N_CONSTANT_APPROVAL: Creation stores a constant true approval/payment flag. A true constant does not verify payment or approval; record the required amount/evidence and the independently authorized decision. This name-based question is advisory.

### N_TRANSITION_BYPASS

N_TRANSITION_BYPASS: A generic enum setter reaches a state also reached by a stricter decision mutation. Apply the decision authority to every path reaching that state; write independent transition intent and run test.

### N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK

N_STALE_CREATION_CHECK: A creator checks a mutable eligibility column that an approval-like transition does not recheck. One question groups the created table, dependency and decision sites; immutable ownership reads and unrelated edits are excluded. Decide whether eligibility must remain current and write independent intent; test create, eligibility change, approval. The named literal-state fragment covers approved/accepted/authorized/granted/issued/active/confirmed/paid/signed and true approval flags; other synonyms are not inferred safe.

### N_DURATION_BOUNDS

N_DURATION_BOUNDS: Operations apply different server-relative duration bounds to one column. Compare the windows with the specification and make them consistent or document deliberate differences.

### N_ROLE_WIDE_WRITE

N_ROLE_WIDE_WRITE: A global role plus viewer attribution does not identify the owner of this resource. Ask whether any role member may write any row; model the target-to-owner relationship and guard it. See the Wall ownership rule recipe.

### E_SECURITY_NOTES

E_SECURITY_NOTES: the individual disposition file is malformed, cannot be written, or sources changed while recording a review. Inspect snapback/security-reviews.json and run check --json for current IDs. Supply a nonempty specification reason for one current note; neither bulk acknowledgments nor this file can clear an actual refutation.

### N_CREATE_EDIT_ASYMMETRY

N_CREATE_EDIT_ASYMMETRY: An argument-supplied column has a specific change guard on edit that creation does not imply. The question names that column, editor and guard, rather than a table-wide permission. Confirm creation authority against the specification; enforce the change guard at creation when required and test independent column write intent with non-null input. Exact changed-field comparisons are supported; mixed conditions, intervening writes and early-return equivalents remain outside this heuristic, with generic insert inventory retained when applicable. Absence of advice is not a safety proof.

### N_PRIVATE_CREATE_EDIT_ASYMMETRY

N_PRIVATE_CREATE_EDIT_ASYMMETRY: A caller can initialize a private column without its change guard and outside its column read audience. This question ranks above ordinary asymmetry because the caller supplies private agency data it cannot read. Confirm who may supply this field at creation; enforce the guard when required and test independent column write intent with a non-null value. Read privacy alone does not define write authority; the question is advisory.

### N_EVIDENCE_REMOVAL

N_EVIDENCE_REMOVAL: Delete, detachment or explicit clearing can remove parent-linked media evidence. The question names removing operations and the parent reference, grouping the evidence columns. Required child fields alone do not require a surviving child; confirm last-child retention against the specification. Guard deletion or detachment transactionally, replace evidence or retire the parent, then declare independent parent integrity intent and run test. Ordinary non-null photo replacement is not removal; optional attachments without required creation linkage or independent integrity intent are excluded. This question is advisory.

# LLP 2000.000: Snapback 3 — keep the core, flip two substrates, start at hub scale

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Draft
**Role:** Second opinion on LLP 2000; since 2026-09-12 also the design brief Snapback 4 builds (LLP 3000)
**Systems:** Snapback 3 product architecture, bounded computation, client data model, client API vocabulary, language and tooling, effects runtime, verification (simulation), performance budgets, process
**Author:** Claude Fable 5.1, at Charlie Cheever's request
**Date:** 2026-09-12
**Revised:** 2026-09-12 (adopted as the Snapback 4 design brief by LLP 3000 decision 3); 2026-09-12 (initial)
**Related:** [LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md) (parent), [LLP 3000](./3000-snapback4.explainer.md) (the Snapback 4 root that builds this brief), LLP 0000, [LLP 0329](./0329-agent-native-rebuild-diagnosis.research.md), [LLP 0329.014.004](./0329.014.004-bounded-data-programs-v1-design.rfc.md), [LLP 0329.016](./0329.016-agentic-dev-loop-from-scratch.rfc.md), [LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md), [LLP 1001](./1001-query-engine.spec.md), [LLP 1002](./1002-dev-loop.spec.md), [LLP 1012](./1012-local-first-v1.spec.md), [LLP 1018.003](./1018.003-truthful-and-composed-client.decision.md), [LLP 1018.008](./1018.008-elegance-after-the-corrections.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.007](./1018.008.007-affordable-offline-acquisition.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.008](./1018.008.008-locality-of-application-changes.research.md), [LLP 1018.008.009](./1018.008.009-residual-ergonomic-gaps.research.md), [LLP 1019](./1019-derived-delivery-custody.rfc.md), [LLP 1020](./1020-day-two-evolution-and-legible-ceilings.rfc.md), [LLP 1023](./1023-clique-builder-jump.rfc.md), [LLP 1024](./1024-single-lane-delivered-search.rfc.md), [LLP 1025](./1025-digest-final-emission-at-hub-scale.research.md), `rules/RULES.md`, `rules/NOT-DOING.md`, `benchmarks/runs/2026-09-05-clique-full-3x3/holistic-scores.md`

## 1. Summary

LLP 2000 is right that the whole application is the unit of design, right
that ownership comes before abstraction, and right to ask for deterministic
simulation and an early real deployment. Its weakness is that it treats the
two structural choices that produced Snapback 2's costs as open research
questions, and then proposes a first experiment at exactly the scale where
those costs are invisible. This document takes a position on both, names
what to keep from Snapback 2 verbatim, and rewrites the first slice so it
can fail for the right reasons.

The position, in one paragraph. Snapback 2's *core* is excellent and should
be copied: the rule language and its uniformity analysis, the structural-fact
family, one data language, typed states with no silence, refusals that paste
a rewrite, personas, the successor classifier, the derived per-recipient
log, the loop verbs and their sub-second budgets. Two *substrates* under
that core are where the record shows the hours went, and both should be
flipped rather than re-investigated: (1) the static certificate should keep
certifying **authorization and shape** and stop pricing **bytes and steps**,
which move to a deterministic runtime meter with honest `capped`/abort
outcomes; and (2) the client should hold **a replica of the viewer's declared
partition** — the local-first shape every shipped sync engine and Snapback
2's own `deliver` log converge on — instead of a per-query result cache
proven by receipts. Those two flips dissolve most of the machinery that
leaked into the application (receipts, coverage, halos, validators, grants,
ID slices, drains, `withHistory`, follower inboxes, per-table retention
words) and turn the 28-second acquisition into a bulk stream whose floor is
the device's write speed. The first slice should be built on the **hub
fixture** (1,000 memberships, 500 follows, 100,000 messages), with the
day-two change designed before the day-one screen, a native client in the
first slice, and a deterministic simulator as the primary test harness.

Three claims this document makes that LLP 2000 does not:

1. **The costs have two named causes, and both are decisions, not
   mysteries.** Byte-priced static certification and the receipt-proven
   result cache account for every ergonomic residual in LLP 1018.008.009
   except documentation. §2 shows the mapping.
2. **The first experiment must include the hub.** Snapback 2 was "elegant on
   day one and hostile on day two" (LLP 1020) and broke at 1,000 memberships
   (LLPs 1023, 1024, 1025). A two-principal slice will pass and teach nothing.
3. **The process is part of the product.** Seventy-one LLPs, over two
   thousand commits, and seven ceiling raises in fourteen days produced a
   sound system nobody can hold in their head. Snapback 3 needs one owner on
   the core, a simulator instead of a test matrix, and budgets anchored to
   competitors so that raising one means admitting a loss.

row below is a Snapback 2 cost recorded in the corpus, with the substrate
that produced it. Numbers are the corpus's own and retain its scope limits.

    fn parse_sync_rest(&mut self, site: Site, audience: SyncAudience, rewrite: &str) -> Fallible<SyncDecl> {
        let mut horizon = None;
        if self.maybe("last") {
            let n = self.number()?;
            if !self.maybe("by") {
                return Err(syntax_with(&site, "a horizon is `last N by index`", rewrite));
            }
            // @ref LLP 3000.019#3.1 — a window can state several ordered columns.
            let order = if self.at(".") {
                let mut columns = Vec::new();
                let mut duplicate = None;
                loop {
                    if !self.maybe(".") || !self.at_kind(Kind::Word) {
                        return Err(syntax_with(&self.peek().site, "each window order column needs a leading dot", "last 500 by .at, .id"));
                    }
                    let column = self.word()?;
                    if columns.contains(&column.value) { duplicate.get_or_insert(column); }
                    else { columns.push(column.value); }
                    if !self.maybe(",") { break; }
                }
                let order = SyncOrder::Columns(columns);
                if let Some(column) = duplicate {
                    return Err(syntax_with(&column.site, format!("window order names .{} twice", column.value), format!("last {n} by {order}")).guide("sync"));
                }
                order
            } else {
                let index = self.word()?;
                if self.at(",") {
                    // `by createdAt, id`: columns written without their dots.
                    let mut columns = vec![index.value.clone()];
                    let mut at = 0;
                    while self.peek_at(at).value == "," && matches!(self.peek_at(at + 1).kind, Kind::Word | Kind::Symbol) {
                        let next = self.peek_at(at + 1);
                        let column = if next.value == "." { self.peek_at(at + 2).value.clone() } else { next.value.clone() };
                        columns.push(column);
                        at += if next.value == "." { 3 } else { 2 };
                    }
                    return Err(syntax_with(&index.site, format!("a window names one index, or columns each with a leading dot; `{}` is followed by an unexpected comma", index.value),
                        format!("last {n} by {}", SyncOrder::Columns(columns))).guide("sync"));
                }
                SyncOrder::Index(index.value)
            };
            horizon = Some((n, order));
        }
        let own_keys = if self.maybe("with") {
            self.take("own")?;
            self.take("keys")?;
            self.take(".")?;
            Some(self.word()?.value)
        } else { None };
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.000.000#2.1 — `sync to .a, .b` is spelled `sync to .a or .b`: the window's columns use commas.
        if matches!(audience, SyncAudience::Column(_) | SyncAudience::Target { .. } | SyncAudience::Union(_)) && horizon.is_none() && self.at(",") {
            let mut arms = vec![audience.arm()];
            let mut at = 1;
            while self.peek_at(at).value == "." && self.peek_at(at + 1).kind == Kind::Word {
                arms.push(format!(".{}", self.peek_at(at + 1).value));
                if self.peek_at(at + 2).value != "," { break; }
                at += 3;
            }
            return Err(syntax_with(&self.peek().site.clone(), format!("the arms of a union audience are joined with `or`, not a comma: `sync to {}`", arms.join(", ")),
                format!("sync to {}  -- each arm is one whole disjunct of the read rule (guide sharing)", arms.join(" or "))).guide("sharing"));
        }
        if !self.at_kind(Kind::Newline) && !self.at_kind(Kind::Eof) {
            let audience_text = match &audience {
                SyncAudience::Public => "sync public".to_owned(),
                SyncAudience::Inferred { .. } => audience.arm(),
                other => format!("sync to {}", other.arm()),
            };
            let written = format!("{audience_text}{}", horizon.as_ref().map(|(n, order)| format!(" last {n} by {order}")).unwrap_or_default());
            return Err(syntax_with(&self.peek().site.clone(), format!("unexpected {} after `{written}`", self.peek().value), format!("end the sync line after `{written}`; a window is `last N by .column, .id` or `last N by indexName`")));
        }
        self.newline()?;
        Ok(SyncDecl { audience, horizon, own_keys, site })
    }

    fn parse_retention(&mut self) -> Fallible<(String, Site)> {
        let site = self.take("retain")?.site;
        let retention = |message: String| Diagnostic::new(&site, "E_QUARRY_RETAIN", message, "retain until-revoked  -- alternatively: retain delivered-history");
        if !self.at_kind(Kind::Word) {
            return Err(retention("retain requires a policy word".into()));
        }
        let policy = self.word()?;
        if policy.value != "until-revoked" && policy.value != "delivered-history" {
            return Err(retention(format!("unknown retention policy {}", policy.value)));
        }
        if !self.at_kind(Kind::Newline) {
            return Err(retention("retain accepts exactly one policy word".into()));
        }
        self.newline()?;
        Ok((policy.value, site))
    }

        self.newline()?;

    fn parse_statement(&mut self) -> Fallible<Stmt> {
        let token = self.peek().clone();
        if token.kind == Kind::Word && self.peek_at(1).value == "=" && self.peek_at(2).value != "=" && reserved::BINDING_WORDS.contains(&token.value.as_str()) {
            return Err(reserved::binding(&token.site, &token.value));
        }
        match token.value.as_str() {
            "while" => return Err(unsupported(&token.site, "while", "use a bounded for domain or walk")),
            "break" => {
                let site = self.take("break")?.site;
                self.newline()?;
                return Ok(Stmt::Break { site });
            }
            "continue" => {
                let site = self.take("continue")?.site;
                self.newline()?;
                return Ok(Stmt::Continue { site });
            }
            "if" => return self.parse_if(),
            "elif" => return Err(unsupported(&token.site, "elif", "else if cond:")),
            "as" => {
                let site = self.take("as")?.site;
                let principal = self.expression(0, &[":"])?;
                self.take(":")?;
                self.newline()?;
                let body = self.parse_block()?;
                return Ok(Stmt::As { principal, body, site });
            }
            "for" => return self.parse_for(),
            "require" => return self.parse_require(),
            "return" => {
                let site = self.take("return")?.site;
                if self.at_kind(Kind::Newline) {
                    self.newline()?;
                    return Ok(Stmt::Return { value: Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Null, site: site.clone() }, site });
                }
                let value = self.expression(0, &["<newline>"])?;
                if !matches!(value, Expr::Merge(_)) {
                    self.newline()?;
                }
                return Ok(Stmt::Return { value, site });
            }
            "emit" => {
                let site = self.take("emit")?.site;
                let effect = self.word()?.value;
                let payload = self.expression(0, &["once", "<newline>"])?;
                let once = if self.maybe("once") { Some(self.expression(0, &["<newline>"])?) } else { None };
                self.newline()?;
                return Ok(Stmt::Emit { effect, payload, once, site });
            }
            "device" | "oblivious" => return Err(unsupported(&token.site, &token.value, "pass an explicit bounded argument to the operation")),
            _ => {}
        }
        if self.at_kind(Kind::Word) && self.peek_at(1).value == "=" {
            let name = self.peek().clone();
            let binding = self.local_name()?;
            self.take("=")?;
            let value = self.expression(0, &["<newline>"])?;
            if !matches!(value, Expr::Merge(_)) {
                self.newline()?;
            }
            return Ok(Stmt::Bind { names: vec![binding], value, site: name.site });
        }
        if self.at("(") && self.tuple_binding_ahead() {
            let site = self.take("(")?.site;
            let mut names = vec![self.local_name()?];
            while self.maybe(",") {
                names.push(self.local_name()?);
            }
            self.take(")")?;
            self.take("=")?;
            let value = self.expression(0, &["<newline>"])?;
            self.newline()?;
            return Ok(Stmt::Bind { names, value, site });
        }
        let value = self.expression(0, &["<newline>"])?;
        if !matches!(value, Expr::Merge(_)) {
            self.newline()?;
        }
        let site = value.site().clone();
        Ok(Stmt::Expr { value, site })
    }

                return Err(type_error(given.site(), format!("{name}'s {} is {}; got {}", declared.name, expected.name(), ty.name()), match (ty.required(), expected.required()) {
                    (Ty::Enum(variants), Ty::Text(max)) if variants.iter().any(|variant| variant.chars().count() > max as usize) => format!("change {name}'s parameter to `{}: {}`; not every variant fits text <={max}", declared.name, ty.name()),
                    _ if ty.is_optional() && !expected.is_optional() => self.parent_rewrite(given).unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{} — require this argument once before calling {name}; absent or hidden rows refuse NOT_FOUND", print::expression(&A::Assert { value: Box::new(given.clone()), code: "NOT_FOUND".into(), message: None, site: given.site().clone() }))),
                    _ => format!("pass {} for {}; a table parameter receives an id when called with a reference, or the same-table row snapshot when called with a row. To read fields from an id, bind `{table}[{}] ! else NOT_FOUND` in the helper; multiline fn bodies need `return value`", expected.name(), declared.name, declared.name, table = match expected.required() { Ty::Ref(t) => t, _ => "<table>".into() }),
                }));
            }
            let runtime = self.temp(&declared.name);
            self.maintenance_scopes.insert(runtime.clone(), format!("helper/{name}/parameter/{}", declared.name));
            out.push(Stmt::Let { name: runtime.clone(), value: expr });
            let fields = if self.lookup_viewer_key(given) { BTreeMap::from([(vec![read_diagnostics::VIEWER_KEY.into()], Ty::Bool)]) } else { BTreeMap::new() };
            bindings.insert(declared.name.clone(), Binding { runtime, ty: expected.clone(), declared: expected, parameter: true, revision: 0, fields, error: None, origins: Vec::new(), inline: None });
        }
        Ok(bindings)
    }

    pub(super) fn fn_call(&mut self, function: &ast::FunctionDecl, args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        let bindings = self.helper_arguments(&function.name, &function.args, args, site, out)?;
        let lookup_points = self.helper_lookup_points(function, args);
        let start = out.len();
        let caller = std::mem::replace(&mut self.scopes, vec![bindings]);
        self.declare(pure_calls::CONSTANTS, Ty::Null);
        for read in lookup_points { self.narrow_lookup_point(&read); }
        let focal = self.focal.take();
        let loops = std::mem::take(&mut self.loops);
        // @ref LLP 3000.019#6 — remove the measured helper/inline placement discrepancy.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.2 — placement inherits caller loops; break/continue stay lexical.
        self.caller_loops += loops;
        let returns = std::mem::take(&mut self.returns);
        self.depth += 1;
        self.call_chain.push((function.name.clone(), site.clone()));
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.2 — helpers expand in the caller's placement; a return exits only this expansion.
        let result = match &function.body {
            ast::FunctionBody::Expression(value) => self.value_of(value, out),
            ast::FunctionBody::Block(statements) => {
                let mut body = setup::Body::default();
                self.block(statements, &mut body, false).and_then(|()| {
                    let ty = self.return_type()?;
                    let result = self.temp("result");
                    self.maintenance_scopes.insert(result.clone(), format!("helper/{}/result", function.name));
                    let done = self.temp("returned");
                    out.push(Stmt::Let { name: result.clone(), value: Expr::Literal(Value::Null) });
                    out.push(Stmt::Let { name: done.clone(), value: Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(false)) });
                    let ownership = setup::helper_ownership(&body);
                    let code = helper_returns(body.code, &result, &done).0;
                    out.extend(setup::Body { code, ownership });
                    Ok((ir::var(&result), ty))
                })
            }
        };
        if let Ok((_, ty)) = &result
            && let Ty::Row(table) | Ty::WriteRow(table) | Ty::Page(table, _) = ty.required()
            && self.schema.receipt_dependencies.contains_key(&table) {
            self.receipt_returns.push((table, function.site.clone()));
        }
        if let Ok((value, _)) = &result {
            self.pure_functions.insert(function.name.clone(), pure_calls::statements(&out[start..]) && pure_calls::expression(value));
        }
        self.depth -= 1;
        self.call_chain.pop();
        self.returns = returns;
        self.loops = loops;
        self.caller_loops -= loops;
        self.scopes = caller;
        if point_facts::writes(&out[start..]) { self.invalidate_points(); }
    }

    pub(super) fn call(&mut self, name: &str, args: &[A], site: &Site, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if let Some(result) = self.job_query_call(name, args, site, out) { return result; }
        // Compiler-only references bypass the function catalog entirely.
        let primitive = name.strip_prefix("$builtin:");
        if primitive.is_none() && let Some(function) = self.catalog.functions.get(name).cloned() {
            return self.fn_call(&function, args, site, out);
        }
        let name = primitive.unwrap_or(name);
        let arity = |n: usize, rewrite: &str| -> Fallible<()> {
            if args.len() != n {
                return Err(type_error(site, format!("{name} takes {n} argument{}; received {}", if n == 1 { "" } else { "s" }, args.len()), rewrite));
            }
            Ok(())
        };
        match name {
            "receiptSettled" if primitive.is_some() => {
                arity(1, "receipt settlement needs a row")?;
                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                let Ty::Row(table) = ty else { return Err(type_error(site, "receipt settlement needs a row", "use a receipt row")); };
                Ok((Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::ReceiptSettled { table }, args: vec![value] }, Ty::Bool))
            }
            super::super::intent_variants::PRESENT => {
                let (value, _) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                Ok((Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(value), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) }, Ty::Bool))
            }
            super::super::intent_variants::SEARCH => {
                let (value, ty) = self.expr(&args[0], out)?;
                if ty.text_max().is_none() { return Err(type_error(site, "matching needs present text", "matching (q ?? '')")); }
                let A::Name { name, .. } = &args[1] else { unreachable!("planned needle binding") };
                let runtime = self.temp("intentNeedle");
//! Lexical statement scopes, flow refinements and helper expansion.

use super::*;

impl Binder<'_> {
    // ----- statements -----

    pub(super) fn block(&mut self, statements: &[S], out: &mut setup::Body, completes: bool) -> Fallible<()> {
        let before = self.visible_bindings();
        self.push_scope();
        let count = statements.len();
        let mut result = Ok(());
        for (index, statement) in statements.iter().enumerate() {
            if let Err(error) = self.statement(statement, out, completes && index + 1 == count) {
                if result.is_ok() { result = Err(error); }
            }
        }
        let after = self.visible_bindings();
        self.pop_scope();
        for (name, mut old) in before {
            let new = &after[&name];
            if old.runtime == new.runtime && old.revision != new.revision {
                self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(name, new.clone());
            } else if old.runtime == new.runtime {
                // Facts added inside a lexical block remain local, while a
                // write's invalidation must reach the enclosing loop header.
                let surviving_fields: BTreeMap<_, _> = old.fields.iter()
                    .filter(|(path, ty)| new.fields.get(*path) == Some(*ty))
                    .map(|(path, ty)| (path.clone(), ty.clone()))
                    .collect();
                if surviving_fields.len() != old.fields.len() {
                    old.fields = surviving_fields;
                    self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(name, old);
                }
            }
        }
        result
    }

    pub(super) fn append_errors(&mut self, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
        for error in self.errors.drain(..) {
            if !diagnostics.contains(&error) { diagnostics.push(error); }
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn record_error(&mut self, error: Diagnostic) {
        if !self.errors.contains(&error) { self.errors.push(error); }
    }

    pub(super) fn statement(&mut self, statement: &S, out: &mut setup::Body, completes: bool) -> Fallible<()> {
        let result = self.statement_inner(statement, out, completes);
        if let Err(error) = &result {
            self.record_error(error.clone());
            if let S::Bind { names, .. } = statement {
                for name in names {
                    if self.binding(name).is_some_and(|binding| binding.parameter) { continue; }
                    let runtime = self.declare(name, Ty::Unknown);
                    let binding = self.scopes.last_mut().unwrap().get_mut(name).unwrap();
                    binding.error = Some(error.clone());
                    out.push(Stmt::Let { name: runtime, value: Expr::Literal(Value::Null) });
                }
            }
        }
        result
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — recursive growth is an assignment failure;
    // an ill-typed value keeps its original expression diagnostic.
    fn assignment_type_error(&self, error: Diagnostic, name: &str, value: &A, site: &Site) -> Diagnostic {
        if self.loops > 0 && error.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && recursive_concat(value, name) {
            recursive_list_error(site, name)
        } else { error }
    }

    fn statement_inner(&mut self, statement: &S, out: &mut setup::Body, completes: bool) -> Fallible<()> {
        match statement {
            S::As { principal, body, site } => self.as_viewer(principal, body, site, out),
            S::Return { value, site } => {
                if self.viewer_depth == Some(self.depth) { return Err(job_reads::diagnostic(site, "E_JOB_VIEWER_FLOW", "return cannot leave an as block", "assign a local inside as, then return outside it")); }
                let prior = std::mem::replace(&mut self.returned_data, self.depth == 0 && self.kind == ProgramKind::Query);
                let result = self.value_of(value, out);
                self.returned_data = prior;
                let (expr, ty) = result?;
                self.returns.push((ty, value.clone()));
                out.push(Stmt::Return(expr));
                Ok(())
            }
            S::Bind { names, value, site } => {
                if names.len() == 2 {
                    return self.tuple_bind(names, value, site, out);
                }
                if names.len() != 1 {
                    return Err(unknown(site, "tuple bindings take exactly two names and sorted(a, b) or divmod(a, b)", "(quotient, remainder) = divmod(dividend, divisor)"));
                }
                let name = &names[0];
                if self.binding(name).is_some_and(|binding| binding.parameter) {
                    return Err(unknown(site, format!("{name} is an argument; locals cannot shadow arguments"), format!("rename the local (for example {name}2)")));
                }
                if let Some(mut binding) = self.binding(name).cloned()
                    && let Ty::List(item, max) = &binding.ty
                    && let A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = value
                    && op == "+" && matches!(left.as_ref(), A::Name { name: source, .. } if source == name)
                    && let A::Array { items, .. } = right.as_ref()
                    && items.len() == 1
                {
                    let (element, ty) = self.value_of(&items[0], out)?;
                    let mut origins = binding.origins.clone();
                    origins.push((Ty::List(Box::new(ty.clone()), 1), value.clone()));
                    let joined = if *max == 0 { ty.clone() } else { item.join_item(&ty).map_err(|error| self.assignment_type_error(self.join_error_many(error.at("[]"), &origins), name, value, site))? };
                    if !ty.assignable_to(&joined) || !item.assignable_to(&joined) {
                        return Err(self.assignment_type_error(type_error(site, format!("{name} holds {}; cannot append {}", item.name(), ty.name()), "append an item of the list's type"), name, value, site));
                    }
                    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — append in place; the heap meter is the accumulated list's bound.
                    binding.ty = Ty::List(Box::new(joined), u32::MAX);
                    binding.origins = origins;
                self.newline()?;
                else_body = self.parse_block()?;
            }
        } else if self.at("elif") {
            return Err(unsupported(&self.peek().site, "elif", "else if cond:"));
        }
        Ok(Stmt::If { condition, then_body, else_body, site })
    }

    fn parse_for(&mut self) -> Fallible<Stmt> {
        let site = self.take("for")?.site;
        let name = self.local_name()?;
        self.take("in")?;
        let domain = self.expression(0, &[":"])?;
        self.take(":")?;
        self.newline()?;
        let body = self.parse_block()?;
        Ok(Stmt::For { name, domain, body, site })
    }

    fn tuple_binding_ahead(&self) -> bool {
        let mut cursor = self.position + 1;
        if self.tokens.get(cursor).is_none_or(|t| t.kind != Kind::Word) {
            return false;
        }
        cursor += 1;
        while self.tokens.get(cursor).is_some_and(|t| t.value == ",") {

**NOT READY.** Reviewed against `01bae70281`, including untracked source, regressions, frozen schemas, and guide changes. Three material defects remain:

1. **Conditional siblings can incorrectly discharge mandatory parent evidence.** [creation_advice.rs:274](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b22-sec7/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/security/creation_advice.rs:274) treats absence of `$advice` guards as unconditional execution. The walker adds no such marker for zero-iteration loops or conditional expressions. A matching sibling inside either can therefore suppress `N_OPTIONAL_UPLOAD_CREATE` while the parent still commits without evidence. The final literal-filter amendment is sound in intent, but its unconditional-discharge requirement is not implemented reliably.

2. **Stale-eligibility suppression does not bind the checked entity or require every relevant column.** [creation_advice.rs:216](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b22-sec7/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/security/creation_advice.rs:216) sets one `rechecked` boolean upon finding any matching column. In 030, checking `operatorFlags[viewer, suspended = true]` suppresses the question just like checking `operatorFlags[app.owner, suspended = true]`, although the former checks the inspector rather than the applicant. Likewise, rechecking one of two mutable eligibility columns hides the unchecked column.

3. **Effectful conditions can become supposedly stable column guards.** [changes.rs:18](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b22-sec7/snapback4/crates/snapback4-lang/src/bind/security/authority_walk/changes.rs:18) ignores `Require.condition` and `If.condition`; `prefix` accepts requirements without checking their effects. A changed-field branch can call a helper that grants the caller an owner role, then require that role. Recovery incorrectly promotes the resulting owner requirement into creation-versus-edit asymmetry, although callers obtain that authority inside the edit. This violates §16.9’s exclusion of unknown effects and intervening writes.

The focused regressions cover the commissioned 003/optionality, 040, grouped 030, private 042/non-null replay, and linked 028 removal cases, but miss these counterexamples. All 17 frozen schema hashes match their manifest.
